breeds.name: Affenpinscher

job.text: The Affenpinscher was developed to kill rats and other pests in German stables.

breeds.home: In a house that pest work can look like a small dog who checks the kitchen for mice and then stays close as a companion.

facts.text: Affenpinschers were bred to kill rats and other pests in German stables of the 1600s.
They were later brought indoors to rid the kitchen of mice.
At night they were bed-warming companions for the lady of the house.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 9-11.5 inches and weight as 7-10 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 1936 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Afghan Hound

job.text: Afghans were developed as fast hunting companions in Asia's mountain kingdoms.

breeds.home: In a house that hunting job can look like a dog who wants room to run and a person to stay near.

facts.text: For centuries Afghans were fast hunting companions and status symbols in Asia's mountain kingdoms.
In the 1800s, English officers brought Afghans to the West.
Some authorities maintain that the Afghan Hound is the oldest breed of purebred dogs.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25-27 inches and weight as 50-60 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 1926 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Airedale Terrier

job.text: Airedales were developed by mill workers in the Aire Valley as all-around terriers.

breeds.home: In a house that mix of work can look like a dog who wants to hunt pests, retrieve, and stay busy with the people nearby.

facts.text: In the mid-1800s, factory hands and mill workers in the Aire Valley crossed several British breeds to create the Airedale.
Earlier dogs of this type were called Working, Waterside, and Bingley Terriers.
Their work has included ratting, retrieving ducks, and herding.
Woodrow Wilson, Warren G Harding, and Calvin Coolidge each kept an Airedale.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23 inches and weight as 50-70 pounds.

breeds.name: Akita

job.text: Akitas were developed in northern Japan as big-game hunters and protectors.

breeds.home: In a house that work can look like a dog who stays close to the family and keeps a watch on the home.

facts.text: Akitas were developed in the Akita prefecture of northern Japan.
They were employed as big-game hunters and protectors.
Helen Keller was given an Akita in 1937.
An Akita named Hachiko waited for 9 years at a Japanese train station for his master, who had died.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 26-28 inches (male), 24-26 inches (female) and weight as 100-130 pounds (male), 70-100 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Alaskan Malamute

job.text: Malamutes were developed as sledge dogs to haul heavy loads over long distances.

breeds.home: In a house that freighting job can look like a strong dog who likes to pull and to stay with the family on long outings.

facts.text: The breed name comes from the Mahlemiut, an Inuit tribe that settled in Kotzebue Sound of northwestern Alaska.
They were created to haul heavy loads at low speeds over long distances.
In the Arctic they also worked as hunting partners and backpack carriers.
In 1933, some Malamutes were chosen to help Admiral Richard Byrd on his Antarctic expedition.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25 inches (male), 23 inches (female) and weight as 85 pounds (male), 75 pounds (female).

breeds.name: American English Coonhound

job.text: Frontiersmen developed this hound to trail and tree raccoons.

breeds.home: In a house that trailing job can look like a dog who follows a scent and uses a loud voice when the nose finds something.

facts.text: Frontiersmen developed them to specialize in trailing and treeing raccoons.
Their lineage goes back to British foxhounds kept on the plantations of George Washington and his Virginia neighbors.
The breed is sometimes called the Redtick Coonhound.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24-26 inches (male), 23-25 inches (female) and weight as 45-65 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 2011 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: American Eskimo Dog

job.text: German farmers brought the dogs that became Eskies to America as all-around farm dogs.

breeds.home: In a house that farm-dog job can look like a bright dog who wants a task and likes to stay involved with the people nearby.

facts.text: German farmers arrived in America in the early 1800s and settled in the Midwest.
They brought the German Spitz, ancestor of the modern Eskie, to use as an all-around farm dog.
The German name was changed to American Eskimo Dog, after a Spitz breeding kennel in Ohio.
One Eskie with the Barnum and Bailey Circus became the first dog to walk a tightrope.

The AKC page for the Standard variety lists height as 9-12 inches (toy), 12-15 inches (miniature), 15-19 inches (Standard) and weight as 6-10 pounds (toy), 10-20 pounds (miniature), 25-35 pounds (standard).

breeds.name: American Foxhound

job.text: American Foxhounds were developed to chase foxes alongside horses.

breeds.home: In a house that hunting job can look like a dog who locks onto a scent and gives a carrying voice while following it.

facts.text: Washington, an avid foxhunter, kept English hounds and interbred them with French hounds from the Marquis de Lafayette.
He did not invent the breed alone, but he was a key player in its development.
The breed was bred to chase a fox, not to kill it, and has always worked closely alongside horses.
The American Foxhound is known for a musical voice, and his bays and howls can carry for miles.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 22-25 inches (male), 21-24 inches (female) and weight as 65-70 pounds (male), 60-65 pounds (female).

breeds.name: American Hairless Terrier

job.text: The American Hairless Terrier began as a hairless offshoot of the Rat Terrier.

breeds.home: In a house that terrier background can look like a compact dog who stays curious about small movement and close to the people at home.

facts.text: Breeding began in the 1970s, when a hairless puppy was born into a litter of midsize Rat Terriers.
Her owners, Edwin and Willie Scott of Trout, Louisiana, named her Josephine.
The breed is a naturally occurring offshoot of the Rat Terrier and the only hairless breed indigenous to the United States.
They are the only hairless breed with normal dentition.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 12-16 inches and weight as 12-28 pounds.

breeds.name: American Pit Bull Terrier

job.text: The American Pit Bull Terrier comes from nineteenth-century crosses of bulldogs and terriers in England, Ireland, and Scotland. In the United States, farmers and ranchers used these dogs to catch semi-wild cattle and hogs, to hunt, and to drive livestock.

breeds.home: At home, a dog bred to catch and drive livestock still wants a physical job. A walk with work in it, and a clear start and finish to that work, fits the original use.

facts.text: UKC history says fanciers in England, Ireland, and Scotland began crossing bulldogs and terriers in the nineteenth century.
Immigrants brought those bull-and-terrier crosses to the United States, where farmers and ranchers used them as catch dogs for semi-wild cattle and hogs, to hunt, and to drive livestock.
The United Kennel Club was the first registry to recognize the American Pit Bull Terrier. Founder C. Z. Bennett assigned registration number 1 to his own dog, Bennett's Ring, in 1898.
The UKC standard describes a medium-sized, short-coated dog whose body is just slightly longer than tall, built as a catch dog that can hold, push, pull, and breathe while working.

The UKC standard gives a desirable weight of 35 to 60 pounds for a mature male and 30 to 50 pounds for a mature female, and a height guide of 18 to 21 inches for males and 17 to 20 inches for females.

breeds.name: American Staffordshire Terrier

job.text: The AmStaff got its start as a fighting and baiting dog of the 18th and 19th centuries.

breeds.home: In a house that old contest work can look like a sturdy dog who wants hard play and stays close to their person.

facts.text: The AmStaff got its start as a fighting and baiting dog of the 18th and 19th centuries.
Those dogs were expected to fight one another or were turned loose in packs against a staked bear or bull.
A dog of this breed named Stubby earned the rank of Sergeant and was the most decorated dog of World War I.
American breeders wanted a heavier dog than the British breed, and the name American Staffordshire Terrier followed.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 18-19 inches (male), 17-18 inches (female) and weight as 55-70 pounds (male), 40-55 pounds (female).

breeds.name: American Water Spaniel

job.text: The American Water Spaniel was developed to hunt waterfowl in and around the Great Lakes.

breeds.home: In a house that hunting job can look like a dog who wants to swim, retrieve, and spend a long day outdoors with their person.

facts.text: European immigrants who settled Wisconsin and Minnesota depended on the region's waterfowl.
It was the first breed developed in the United States as an all-around hunter that could retrieve from boats.
The breed was named the state dog of Wisconsin in 1986.
Over generations they used European breeds to create the AWS for hunting in and around the Great Lakes.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 15-18 inches and weight as 30-45 pounds (male), 25-40 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Anatolian Shepherd Dog

job.text: Sheep and goat herders in Anatolia developed this dog as a livestock guardian.

breeds.home: In a house that guardian job can look like a large dog who watches the yard and the household.

facts.text: Anatolia, or Asia Minor, is the peninsula that makes up the Asian portion of Turkey.
Sheep and goat herders developed a livestock guardian called the coban kopegi, forerunner of the Anatolian Shepherd.
The breed is also known as Goban Kopegi, Anatolian Karabash, or Kangal.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 29 inches (male), 27 inches (female) and weight as 110-150 pounds (male), 80-120 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 1996 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Australian Cattle Dog

job.text: Australian Cattle Dogs were developed to work cattle for farmers.

breeds.home: In a house that cattle work can look like a dog who watches movement, heels in close, and wants a job to finish.

facts.text: In the 1800s, George Elliot bred Dingoes with Collies and sold the puppies to farmers.
Jack and Harry Bagust later bred Dalmatians with some of those dogs.
A sheepdog was also added to the line.
The breed was first known as the Australian Heeler and is still called the Blue or Queensland Heeler.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 18-20 inches (male), 17-19 inches (female) and weight as 35-50 pounds.

breeds.name: Australian Shepherd

job.text: Australian Shepherds were developed as sheepdogs and later refined on American ranches.

breeds.home: In a house that herding job can look like a dog who wants to gather the family and keep everyone moving the same way.

facts.text: The breed's story starts in Europe near the Pyrenees, where the Basques had long been known as shepherds.
In the 1800s Basques and their dogs sailed east to try their luck in Australia.
The Basques left Australia for California, where ranchers assumed the dogs were an Australian breed, and the misleading name Australian Shepherd followed.
Aussies were refined in America and became part of cowboy culture.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 20-23 inches (male), 18-21 inches (female) and weight as 50-65 pounds (male), 40-55 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Australian Terrier

job.text: Australian Terriers were bred to work on small mammals and snakes.

breeds.home: In a house that exterminator job can look like a small dog who investigates holes and small animals, then settles in as a companion.

facts.text: The breed is said to come from crosses of British terriers, including the Cairn, Dandie Dinmont, Norwich, Scottie, Skye, and Yorkie.
They worked on small mammals and snakes.
One of the smallest working terriers, they were bred as both helper and companion in rough times and terrain.
The Australian Terrier was the first Australian breed recognized and shown in its native land.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10-11 inches and weight as 15-20 pounds.

breeds.name: Azawakh

job.text: Azawakhs were expected to guard the camels and goats of nomads in the Sahel.

breeds.home: In a house that guarding job can look like a lean dog who watches the people and the yard.

facts.text: The breed is associated with the nomad tribes of the Sahel and is named for the Azwakh Valley.
They were expected to protect the camels and goats the nomads depended on in the Sahara.
Built along Greyhound lines, an Azawakh can reach 35 mph on the straightaway.
The Azawakh is also known as the Tuareg Sloughi and has been a companion of the nomads of the South Sahara for hundreds of years.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25-29 inches (male), 23.5-27.5 inches (female) and weight as 44-55 pounds (male), 33-44 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Barbet

job.text: The Barbet was developed as a water dog for hunting water game in France.

breeds.home: In a house that water-dog job can look like a dog who wants to swim, retrieve, and come home muddy.

facts.text: The Barbet was originally a water dog, used in France mainly for hunting water game.
Some experts call the Barbet an ancestor of the Poodle and the Irish Water Spaniel.
The Barbet was a hunting companion of Henri IV and Louis XV.
The name comes from the French barbe, meaning beard.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 19-24.5 inches and weight as 35-65 pounds.

breeds.name: Basenji

job.text: Basenjis were prized in Africa as hunters who used sight, speed, and scent.

breeds.home: In a house that hunting job can look like a dog who watches, leaps, and follows whatever is moving.

facts.text: Basenjis were brought up the Nile from interior Africa as gifts for the pharaohs of ancient Egypt.
They are depicted in Egyptian artifacts that are 4,500 years old.
African tribesmen prized them as hunters with keen eyesight, speed, and a strong sense of smell.
The Basenji does not bark, makes yodeling noises, and is known as the barkless dog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 17 inches (male), 16 inches (female) and weight as 24 pounds (male), 22 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Basset Fauve de Bretagne

job.text: The Basset Fauve was developed as a shorter-legged hound for hunters who did not have horses.

breeds.home: In a house that hunting job can look like a dog who follows a scent close to the ground and likes to range nearby.

facts.text: The breed traces to the 1500s, when Francois I hunted with a pack of Breton hounds.
Those earlier dogs were Grand Fauve de Bretagne, a breed that later became extinct.
Most peasants did not own a horse, so they needed a shorter-legged, close-ranging hunting companion.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 12.5-15.5 inches and weight as 23-39 pounds.
The AKC breeds-by-year list gives 2026 as the year this breed became registrable.

breeds.name: Basset Hound

job.text: Basset Hounds were bred in France as low-slung hounds to track rabbits and deer.

breeds.home: In a house that trailing job can look like a dog who follows a scent slowly and stays with it until the trail is done.

facts.text: The name comes from French: basset means low, and the breed was developed in France and Belgium.
Friars of the Abbey of St. Hubert are thought to have crossed strains of older French breeds.
The Marquis de Lafayette brought Bassets to America and gave a pack to George Washington.
In trailing, the Basset's nose is said to be second only to the Bloodhound.
The AKC breed standard lists height as up to 15 inches and weight as 40-65 pounds.

breeds.name: Beagle

job.text: Beagles were developed in England as small hounds to track rabbits.

breeds.home: In a house that trailing job can look like a dog who puts their nose down and follows a scent until it runs out.

facts.text: By the 1500s, English gentlemen kept smaller hounds to track rabbits, and those compact hounds were the first Beagles.
Some experts say the name comes from the Gaelic word beag, meaning little.
There are reports of hounds used for hunting in England even before the Romans arrived in 55 b.c.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 13 inches & under, 13-15 inches and weight as under 20 pounds (13 inches & under), 20-30 pounds (13-15 inches).
The American Kennel Club lists 1885 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Bearded Collie

job.text: Beardies were developed in Scotland to herd cattle and drive the herd to market.

breeds.home: In a house that droving job can look like a dog who wants to move the family along and keep the group together.

facts.text: Shepherds prized Beardies for herding and droving in Scotland's raw climate and hilly terrain.
They were expected to help control cattle at pasture and drive the herd to market.
A prevailing belief is that Beardies descend from Polish Lowland Sheepdogs brought to Scotland in the 1500s.
The Beardie is also known as the Highland Collie, the Mountain Collie, or the Hairy Mou'ed Collie.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 21-22 inches (male), 20-21 inches (female) and weight as 45-55 pounds.

breeds.name: Beauceron

job.text: Beaucerons were developed in the Beauce region of France to move livestock.

breeds.home: In a house that herding job can look like a calm dog who watches the household and steps in when the group should move.

facts.text: The name comes from Beauce, a vast agricultural region southwest of Paris.
The breed is also known as the Berger de Beauce or the Bas Rouge.
Since the late Middle Ages they have moved livestock, and they have also served as soldiers, bodyguards, and rescuers.
Beaucerons served the French cause during both world wars.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25.5-27.5 inches (male), 24-26.5 inches (female) and weight as 70-110 pounds.

breeds.name: Bedlington Terrier

job.text: Bedlingtons were developed in a northern mining district to kill rats in coal mines and hunt varmints.

breeds.home: In a house that ratting job can look like a dog who checks corners and small spaces, then settles in with the household.

facts.text: Bedlingtons were employed as coal-mine ratters and varmint killers.
A dog called the gypsy dog came to the attention of Lord Rothbury of Bedlington in Northumberland County.
The first dog called a Bedlington Terrier was Ainsley's Piper, whelped in 1825.
Joseph Ainsley of Bedlington owned the first dog known to be called a Bedlington Terrier.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 15-17.5 inches and weight as 17-23 pounds.

breeds.name: Belgian Laekenois

job.text: Belgian farmers developed the Laekenois to drive and protect livestock.

breeds.home: In a house that farm job can look like a dog who watches the family, moves them along, and stays alert to the yard.

facts.text: Old-time Belgian farmers were preoccupied with dogs that could drive and protect livestock.
The Laekenois is named for the Chateau de Laeken.
Queen Marie-Henriette, born in 1836, was said to favor the breed.
The breed is also known as Laekense and Chien de Berger Belge.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24-26 inches (male), 22-24 inches (female) and weight as 55-65 pounds.

breeds.name: Belgian Malinois

job.text: The Malinois was developed around the city of Malines as a livestock herding dog.

breeds.home: In a house that herding job can look like a busy dog who wants a task and likes to work beside their person.

facts.text: The Malinois was bred around the city of Malines, and the name comes from that city.
It is one of four closely related Belgian herding breeds.
Malinois first came to America in 1911.
They are sought after today as police and military K-9s.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24-26 inches (male), 22-24 inches (female) and weight as 60-80 pounds (male), 40-60 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Belgian Sheepdog

job.text: Belgian Sheepdogs were developed as herding dogs for Belgian farms.

breeds.home: In a house that herding job can look like a dog who keeps an eye on the family and wants work to do.

facts.text: Old-time Belgian farmers were preoccupied with herding.
By the 1890s, four Belgian shepherd types remained: the Belgian Sheepdog, Malinois, Tervuren, and Laekenois.
The longhaired black dogs largely trace to Nicolas Rose and a foundation pair he purchased.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24-26 inches (male), 22-24 inches (female) and weight as 55-75 pounds (male), 45-60 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 1912 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Belgian Tervuren

job.text: Tervurens were developed as all-purpose farm dogs in the village of Tervuren.

breeds.home: In a house that farm job can look like a dog who wants to herd, watch, and stay busy with their person.

facts.text: In Belgium they are known as the Chien de Berger Belge, and they worked as do-it-all dogs on pre-industrial farms.
Around the turn of the 20th century, breeder M.F. Corbeel in the village of Tervuren crossed black dogs and fawn dogs.
The painter A. Clarys featured a Terv in a painting from the very early 20th century.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24-26 inches (male), 22-24 inches (female) and weight as 55-75 pounds (male), 45-60 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 1959 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Bergamasco Sheepdog

job.text: Bergamascos were developed to move and guard sheep on rocky Alpine slopes.

breeds.home: In a house that sheepdog job can look like a dog who watches the household and likes to keep the family group together.

facts.text: The breed has been associated with the town of Bergamo, near Milan, for many centuries.
They are thought to come from Persian stock.
They were among breeds traded around the Mediterranean by the Phoenicians.
They are suited to move and guard sheep on rocky Alpine slopes.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23.5 inches (male), 22 inches (female) and weight as 70-84 pounds (male), 57-71 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Berger Picard

job.text: The Berger Picard was developed by French shepherds as a pasture herding dog.

breeds.home: In a house that herding job can look like a dog who wants to gather people and pets and keep an eye on the household.

facts.text: The Picard is thought to be the oldest of the pasture dogs developed by French shepherds.
This herder was brought to northern France, then called Gaul, by invading Celts in the third century b.c.
Two world wars nearly rendered the Picard extinct.
Berger Picards were shown in the same class as Beaucerons and Briards in 1863.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23.5-25.5 inches (male), 21.5-23.5 inches (female) and weight as 50-70 pounds.

breeds.name: Bernese Mountain Dog

job.text: Bernese Mountain Dogs were developed as Swiss farm dogs to pull carts and drive dairy cattle.

breeds.home: In a house that farm job can look like a dog who likes to pull, stays near the family, and keeps an eye on the home.

facts.text: They originated in Switzerland and are named for the Canton of Bern.
Farm work for them included pulling carts.
They also drove dairy cattle and watched the farm.
Ancestors of the Bernese were brought into Switzerland more than two thousand years ago by invading Roman soldiers.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25-27.5 inches (male), 23-26 inches (female) and weight as 80-115 pounds (male), 70-95 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Bichon Frise

job.text: Bichons first worked with Spanish sailors and later became companion dogs.

breeds.home: In a house that companion role looks like a small dog who stays close, picks up tricks, and wants to be part of the day.

facts.text: The breed first worked on the high seas with Spanish sailors.
They were companions to Italian nobility in the 1300s.
They later traveled with organ grinders and circus acts and learned tricks quickly.
The Bichon made its appearance in France under Francis I.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 9.5-11.5 inches and weight as 12-18 pounds.

breeds.name: Biewer Terrier

job.text: The Biewer Terrier was developed in Germany from Yorkshire Terriers as a small companion dog.

breeds.home: In a house that companion role looks like a very small dog who wants to be with the people they live with.

facts.text: The breed originated in Germany in 1984, when two tricolor puppies were born to Yorkshire Terrier breeders Werner and Gertrude Biewer.
A famous German singer took a liking to the dogs and added the words a la Pom Pon to the breed name.
The breed's original name was German Yorkshire Terrier.
American fanciers began importing the breed from Germany in 2002.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 7-11 inches and weight as 4-8 pounds.

breeds.name: Black and Tan Coonhound

job.text: Black and Tan Coonhounds were developed to trail raccoons by scent and tree them for hunters.

breeds.home: In a house that trailing job can look like a dog who follows a scent with nose down and gives voice when the quarry is found.

facts.text: Frontiersmen crossed European hounds to create the coonhound.
These dogs trail raccoon scent through woods and swamps until they tree the quarry.
They bawl in a clear voice so hunters can find them.
The Black and Tan is believed to come from Bloodhounds and Foxhounds.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25-27 inches (male), 23-25 inches (female) and weight as 65-110 pounds.

breeds.name: Black Russian Terrier

job.text: The Black Russian Terrier was developed by the Soviet military as a multi-purpose military dog.

breeds.home: In a house that military-dog job can look like a large dog who wants a task, stays with their people, and watches the home.

facts.text: In the late 1940s the Soviet Red Star Kennel began a program to develop a multi-purpose military dog.
More than 17 breeds were used, including the Giant Schnauzer, Airedale, Rottweiler, Newfoundland, and Russian Ovcharka.
The first standard for the Black Terrier was published in 1958.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 27-30 inches (male), 26-29 inches (female) and weight as 80-130 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 2004 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Bloodhound

job.text: Bloodhounds were developed to follow human scent and find people who are lost or hiding.

breeds.home: In a house that trailing job can look like a dog who lives through their nose and will follow a scent until they sort it out.

facts.text: Bloodhounds as we know them were perfected in Western Europe about a thousand years ago.
Police departments have relied on them to follow human scent.
In his Historia Animalium, the third-century scholar Aelian mentions a hound of unrivaled scenting powers.
The first specimens were brought from Constantinople in two strains, black and white.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25-27 inches (male), 23-25 inches (female) and weight as 90-110 pounds (male), 80-100 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Bluetick Coonhound

job.text: Blueticks were developed as scenthounds, and today's dogs specialize in trailing raccoons.

breeds.home: In a house that scent work can look like a dog who puts their nose down and follows a trail until they find what they were after.

facts.text: Blueticks and the other coonhound breeds are scenthounds.
Long ago Blueticks trailed big game, and today's dogs specialize on the raccoon.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 22-27 inches (male), 21-25 inches (female) and weight as 55-80 pounds (male), 45-65 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 2009 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Boerboel

job.text: Boerboels were developed in South Africa as farm dogs to guard remote homesteads from predators.

breeds.home: In a house that guardian job can look like a large dog who watches the property and stays with the people who live there.

facts.text: Boer, a Dutch word meaning farmer, was the name given to Dutch, German, and Huguenot settlers of South Africa who began arriving in the mid-1600s.
To protect remote homesteads from predators, they brought large guarding dogs, the Bullmastiff among them.
Crosses of European bloodlines in South Africa gave rise to the Boerboel.
The word Boerboel means Farm Dog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24-27 inches (male), 22-25 inches (female) and weight as 150-200 pounds.

breeds.name: Border Collie

job.text: Border Collies were developed in the borderland between England and Scotland to herd sheep.

breeds.home: In a house that herding job can look like a dog who watches movement, gathers the family, and wants a task to work.

facts.text: The breed comes from the borderland between England and Scotland.
Long-ago breeders of the British Isles crossed native stock with dogs brought by invading Romans and Vikings.
Collie is a Scottish dialect word for sheepdogs, including Border Collies.
The Border Collie was first classified as the Scotch Sheep Dog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 19-22 inches (male), 18-21 inches (female) and weight as 30-55 pounds.

breeds.name: Border Terrier

job.text: Border Terriers were developed to follow foxhounds and bolt foxes from their lairs.

breeds.home: In a house that terrier job can look like a small dog who wants to dig, follow a scent, and check every hole.

facts.text: Farmers and shepherds near the Scottish-English border developed them to pursue the sheep-stealing fox.
They needed legs long enough to keep up with foxhounds and huntsmen on horseback.
They also had to be small enough to dig into the fox's lair and force the fox into the open.
Their value to farmers rested on bolting foxes and controlling vermin.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 12-15 inches and weight as 13-15.5 pounds (male), 11.5-14 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Borzoi

job.text: Borzoi were developed by the Russian aristocracy to hunt wolves.

breeds.home: In a house that hunting job can look like a tall dog who wants room to run and a person to stay near afterward.

facts.text: Under Romanov rule, wolf hunting was a passion of the Russian aristocracy.
The Borzoi began in 17th-century Russia, when Arabian greyhounds were crossed with a thick-coated Russian breed.
The first Borzoi standard was written in 1650.
The 1917 Russian Revolution brought the killing of the nobility and their hounds.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 28 inches & up (male), 26 inches & up (female) and weight as 75-105 pounds (male), 60-85 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Boston Terrier

job.text: The Boston Terrier was developed in Boston from a Bulldog and English Terrier cross.

breeds.home: In a house that companion role looks like a compact dog who lives close to the people around them.

facts.text: Sometime around 1870, Robert C. Hooper of Boston acquired Judge, a cross between a Bulldog and an English Terrier.
Judge has been called the ancestor of all true modern Bostons.
A gentle nature earned the breed the nickname The American Gentleman.
The Boston Terrier is a native American breed.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10-12 inches and weight as 12-25 pounds.

breeds.name: Bouvier des Flandres

job.text: The Bouvier was developed in Flanders to move cattle.

breeds.home: In a house that cattle-driving job can look like a strong dog who likes to herd, pull, and keep watch over the household.

facts.text: Bouvier des Flandres roughly means cowherd of Flanders, and moving cattle was once the main work.
They also pulled carts, and in World War I they served as messengers and ambulance dogs.
In medieval times Flanders covered parts of today's France, Belgium, and the Netherlands.
Other names include Vuilbaard, koehond, and toucheur de boeuf.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24.5-27.5 inches (male), 23.5-26.5 inches (female) and weight as 70-110 pounds.

breeds.name: Boxer

job.text: The modern Boxer was developed in Germany from the Bullenbeisser and worked as a cattle dog, police dog, and war dog.

breeds.home: In a house that working background can look like an energetic dog who wants a job and stays in the middle of family life.

facts.text: Boxer ancestors used as war dogs go back as far as 2,500 b.c.
The modern Boxer traces to Germany in the late 1800s and is thought to have been bred down from the Bullenbeisser.
Boxers have worked as cattle dogs, police dogs, war dogs, and guide dogs for the blind.
Flemish tapestries of the 16th and 17th centuries show Boxer ancestors in stag and boar hunts.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23-25 inches (male), 21.5-23.5 inches (female) and weight as 65-80 pounds (male), females are about 15 pounds less than male.

breeds.name: Boykin Spaniel

job.text: The Boykin Spaniel was developed in South Carolina as a small hunting spaniel.

breeds.home: In a house that hunting job can look like a compact dog who wants to retrieve and stay close enough to go along in the boat.

facts.text: Around 1900, Whit Boykin of Camden, South Carolina, took in a brown spaniel named Dumpy who proved to be an excellent hunter.
Boykin crossed Dumpy with various spaniel breeds and came to the gundog that bears his name.
The Boykin Spaniel is the official dog of South Carolina.
The breed is small enough that a hunter can lift both dog and duck into a boat at the same time.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 15.5-18 inches (male), 14-16.5 inches (female) and weight as 30-40 pounds (male), 25-35 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Bracco Italiano

job.text: The Bracco Italiano was developed in northern Italy as a pointing dog.

breeds.home: In a house that gundog job can look like a dog who ranges out, stops on point, and wants a long day in the field.

facts.text: The Bracco Italiano has been called the oldest European pointer, with a history back to the fourth or fifth century BC.
It is generally accepted that the breed began as a cross between the Segugio Italiano and the Asiatic Mastiff.
One variety, white and orange, is associated with Piedmont, and the roan and brown variety with Lombardy.
The breed was bred by the Gonzaga and Medici families.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 21-27 inches and weight as 55-90 pounds.

breeds.name: Briard

job.text: Briards were developed in the Brie region of France to herd sheep and guard the flock.

breeds.home: In a house that farm job can look like a dog who wants to herd the household and keep an eye on the yard.

facts.text: Briards are named for the region of Brie and have worked pastures in northern France since Charlemagne's time.
In early times Briards were used to defend their charges against wolves and poachers.
Thomas Jefferson and the Marquis de Lafayette introduced Briards to America.
Napoleon, who did not particularly like dogs, was a fan of the breed.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23-27 inches (male), 22-25.5 inches (female) and weight as 55-100 pounds.

breeds.name: Brittany

job.text: Brittanys were developed in Brittany, France, as gundogs with a nose for birds.

breeds.home: In a house that gundog job can look like a busy dog who wants to range, point, and hunt birds with their person.

facts.text: The breed is named for Brittany, the westernmost region of France, between the English Channel and the Bay of Biscay.
American-style Brittanys are considered more pointers than spaniels.
They are versatile gundogs prized for stamina and a strong nose for birds.
The first Brittany standard was outlined in 1907, and the breed was introduced to the United States in 1931.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 17.5-20.5 inches and weight as 30-40 pounds.

breeds.name: Brussels Griffon

job.text: Brussels Griffons were developed to catch rats in the stables of horse-drawn cabs.

breeds.home: In a house that ratting job can look like a small dog who checks corners and wants to go along with their person.

facts.text: Developed in Brussels, they were bred from the Affenpinscher, a Belgian street dog, the Pug, and the Ruby Spaniel.
They were used to catch rats in the stables of horse-drawn cabs and often rode beside the driver.
The street-dog side of the cross was called Griffons d'Ecurie, or Stable Griffons.
Van Eyck's 1434 portrait of the Arnolfini Couple includes a distant ancestor of the breed.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 7-10 inches and weight as 8-10 pounds.

breeds.name: Bull Terrier

job.text: James Hinks developed the modern Bull Terrier in the early 1860s from the Bull-and-Terrier.

breeds.home: In a house that sporting-dog background can look like a sturdy dog who wants hard play and stays close to their person.

facts.text: James Hinks took a Bulldog-terrier cross called the Bull-and-Terrier and refined it into the modern Bull Terrier.
Hinks's dogs were white, and colored dogs appeared by the early 20th century.
In the early 1900s, Bull Terriers were crossed back to brindle Staffordshires to produce a colored variety.
Bulldog-terrier crosses became popular as sporting dogs in the early 1800s.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 21-22 inches and weight as 50-70 pounds.

breeds.name: Bulldog

job.text: Bulldogs were created in England for the sport of bullbaiting.

breeds.home: In a house this former bullbaiting dog lives beside the people of the home.

facts.text: Historical evidence places the Bulldog's creation in 13th-century England, during the reign of King John, for bullbaiting.
In that sport a staked bull faced a pack of dogs while spectators bet on the outcome.
In 1835, England banned blood sports, a turning point for the breed.
President Calvin Coolidge owned a Bulldog named Boston Beans.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 14-15 inches and weight as 50 pounds (male), 40 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Bullmastiff

job.text: The Bullmastiff was developed in England as the gamekeeper's night dog to catch poachers.

breeds.home: In a house that night-dog job can look like a large dog who watches the home and stays between the family and anything out of place.

facts.text: In the 1800s the breed was developed by combining the Mastiff and the Bulldog.
They were called the gamekeeper's night dog and used against poachers.
The Bullmastiff would knock a poacher down and hold him, without biting, until a groundskeeper arrived.
The known history of the Bullmastiff begins about 1860 in England.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25-27 inches (male), 24-26 inches (female) and weight as 110-130 pounds (male), 100-120 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Cairn Terrier

job.text: The Cairn Terrier was developed by Scottish farmers to dig into cairns and drive out the animals living in them.

breeds.home: In a house, that digging work can look like a dog who wants to investigate holes, corners, and anything that rustles. A walk with room to sniff and poke around gives the old farm job somewhere to go.

facts.text: Scottish farmers developed the Cairn to dig into cairns and rout out the animals living there.
The breed began in the Western Isles of Scotland, where it was used for centuries as a working terrier.
It was once known as the Short-haired Skye Terrier.
Farms that kept several Cairns were free of rats, mice, moles, and other burrowing animals.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10 inches (male), 9.5 inches (female) and weight as 14 pounds (male), 13 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Canaan Dog

job.text: The Canaan Dog herded flocks for the ancient Israelites.

breeds.home: At home, that shepherding work can look like a dog who stays near its people and keeps track of the household. A family to follow, and a place to watch from, gives the old herding job a daily shape.

facts.text: Among the ancient Israelites, shepherding was an important job.
When the Romans drove the Israelites from the Holy Land in a.d. 70, their herding dogs took refuge in the Negev Desert.
The breed is named for the territory that is today Israel, Lebanon, and parts of the bordering countries.
Drawings on the tombs at Beni-Hassan, from 2200 to 2000 BC, show dogs that look much like the Canaan Dog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 20-24 inches (male), 19-23 inches (female) and weight as 45-55 pounds (male), 35-45 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Cane Corso

job.text: The Cane Corso was developed in Italy as a boar hunter, farm dog, and guardian, and the name roughly means bodyguard dog.

breeds.home: In a house, that guardian work can look like a dog who stays near the family and notices who comes and goes. A clear place in the household, and a person to accompany, gives the old bodyguard role a daily shape.

facts.text: The mollosus dogs are named for the Molossi, an ancient Greek tribe thought to have bred big guardian dogs.
Roman legions brought mollosian dogs to Italy, bred them to native Italian dogs, and produced the Corso and the larger Neapolitan Mastiff.
The original dogs were used as boar hunters, farm dogs, and guardians.
The breed name roughly translates from Latin as bodyguard dog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25-27.5 inches (male), 23.5-26 inches (female) and weight as Proportionate to height.

breeds.name: Cardigan Welsh Corgi

job.text: The Cardigan Welsh Corgi was developed to heel livestock, moving cattle by nipping at their heels.

breeds.home: Around the house, that heeling work can look like a dog who follows close behind and may nip at heels when everyone is on the move. A walk with a person to follow gives the old cattle job a quieter version.

facts.text: The Cardigan is best known as a heeler, a dog that moves cows by nipping at their heels.
The breed is named for the medieval kingdom of Cardiganshire in Wales.
The Cardigan comes from the same line of dogs as the Dachshund.
The two corgis were treated as one breed in Britain until 1934.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10.5-12.5 inches and weight as 30-38 pounds (male), 25-34 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Cavalier King Charles Spaniel

job.text: The Cavalier King Charles Spaniel was a toy spaniel kept as a close companion, most famously by King Charles II.

breeds.home: In a house, that companion role looks like a dog who wants to be at someone's feet and included in the day. A lap, a chair nearby, and time with people is the household version of that old habit.

facts.text: King Charles II owned several toy spaniels and was rarely seen without them at his feet.
He wrote a decree that let his dogs into any public place, including the House of Parliament.
King Charles I and his son Charles II were especially devoted to a black and tan toy spaniel.
When the House of Stuart fell, a link to King Charles's dogs became a political liability, and the breed became very rare.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 12-13 inches and weight as 13-18 pounds.

breeds.name: Cesky Terrier

job.text: The Cesky Terrier was developed to hunt rats like a terrier and to work in packs like a hound.

breeds.home: At home, that mix can look like a dog who wants to investigate small rustles and then settle in with people. A short hunt around the yard, followed by a calm return indoors, echoes the work the breed was made for.

facts.text: The breed came from the vision of one person, the Czech breeder, sportsman, and geneticist Frantisek Horak.
His aim was a dog that could rat like a terrier, work in packs like a hound, and be gentle and obedient at home.
He made the breed by crossing Scottish terriers and Sealyham terriers.
The breed is also called the Czech Terrier or the Bohemian Terrier.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10-13 inches and weight as 14-24 pounds.

breeds.name: Chesapeake Bay Retriever

job.text: The Chesapeake Bay Retriever was bred to retrieve waterfowl from the cold, rough waters of the Chesapeake Bay.

breeds.home: In a house, that retrieving work can look like a dog who wants to swim, carry things, and keep going. A retrieve game and time in the water give the bay retriever's work a place off the marsh.

facts.text: The Chesapeake Bay holds a third of the migratory waterfowl that winter in the East.
The retriever was bred with an insulated coat, a strong body, and large webbed feet so it could swim against ice and wind.
Owners of duck clubs on both shores of the bay set the breed's basic type in the 19th century.
The breed originated in the United States.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23-26 inches (male), 21-24 inches (female) and weight as 65-80 pounds (male), 55-70 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Chihuahua

job.text: The Chihuahua was kept as a close companion.

breeds.home: At home, that companion role looks like a small dog who wants to stay near its person. A lap and a quiet place close by are the household version of a dog kept near its people.

facts.text: The breed takes its name from the Mexican state of Chihuahua, where the earliest known dogs of this type were found.
Ancient paintings in Mexico show dogs that look like the modern Chihuahua.
The dogs appear in ancient stone carvings, and mummies of them have been found buried with their masters.
The breed is most likely related to the Techichis, dogs of Central American Indians, and to the Mexican hairless dog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 5-8 inches and weight as not exceeding 6 pounds.

breeds.name: Chinese Crested

job.text: The Chinese Crested was kept aboard ships to catch rats.

breeds.home: In a house, that ratting work can look like a dog who notices small movement and wants to investigate it. A home to patrol, and a person to follow from room to room, gives the old shipboard job a tame outlet.

facts.text: Large hairless dogs are thought to have been brought from Africa to China and then bred smaller.
Chinese sailors traveled the high seas with these dogs on board.
An earlier name for the breed was the Chinese Ship Dog.
The dogs became known as shipboard rat catchers and were traded among sailors in seaports.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 11-13 inches and weight as 8-12 pounds.

breeds.name: Chinese Shar-Pei

job.text: The Chinese Shar-Pei was used in China to hunt, herd, and guard.

breeds.home: At home, those old roles can look like a dog who watches the door and stays aware of the household. A steady place in the family gives that work a daily form.

facts.text: The Shar-Pei goes back 2,000 years and was used across many eras.
Those uses include guarding, hunting, and herding.
Ancient statues look much like the Shar-Pei, and Chinese manuscripts mention wrinkled dogs.
Like the Chow Chow, the Shar-Pei has a blue-black tongue, a trait shared by only these two breeds.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 18-20 inches and weight as 45-60 pounds.

breeds.name: Chinook

job.text: The Chinook was developed as a sled dog to haul freight.

breeds.home: In a house, that sledding work can look like a dog who wants to pull and to stay with its people on a long outing. A harness walk gives the freighting job a home-sized version.

facts.text: Arthur Walden of Wonalancet, New Hampshire, founded the breed in the years before World War I.
His foundation dogs were a mastiff-type dog and descendants of one of Admiral Peary's Greenland huskies.
He named the breed for Chinook, his lead sled dog, and every Chinook traces back to that dog.
In 1927 Arthur Walden and 16 male Chinooks went with Admiral Richard Byrd on his first expedition to Antarctica.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24-26 inches (male), 22-24 inches (female) and weight as 55-90 pounds (male), 50-65 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Chow Chow

job.text: The Chow Chow was used in China as a hunter, herder, hauler, and guardian.

breeds.home: At home, those roles can look like a dog who watches the house and is ready to go along when the household moves. A steady routine, with something to keep an eye on, fits that old mix of work.

facts.text: A Han Dynasty bas-relief places the Chow as a hunting dog in China in that period.
The breed was used as a guardian, herder, hauler, and hunter.
An ancient nickname for the breed is the Edible Dog.
Distant ancestors of the Chow were used as food.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 17-20 inches and weight as 45-70 pounds.

breeds.name: Cirneco dell'Etna

job.text: The Cirneco was developed to hunt wild rabbits on the rocky slopes of Mount Etna.

breeds.home: In a house, that rabbit hunting can look like a dog who wants to follow a scent and stretch into a run. A long outing with room to course gives the old hunting work somewhere to go.

facts.text: The name Cirneco comes from a Greek word meaning dog of Cyrene, in Libya.
For thousands of years these dogs have chased rabbits on the rocky slopes of Mount Etna, Europe's largest active volcano.
The breed was selected over centuries as a specialist for hunting wild rabbit, mainly by scent.
In the hunt it also uses hearing and sight.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 18-20 inches (male), 17-19 inches (female) and weight as 20-28 pounds (male), 19-25 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Clumber Spaniel

job.text: The Clumber Spaniel was developed as a hunting spaniel for heavy cover.

breeds.home: At home, that hunting work can look like a dog who wants to push through thick brush and search out a scent. A walk in rough cover gives the old spaniel job a place to go.

facts.text: A reliable record of the breed picks up in the late 1700s at Nottingham, England.
The Duke of Newcastle and his gamekeeper perfected the spaniel and named it for his estate, Clumber Park.
The Clumber is thought to be one of the earliest spaniels developed for a special use, and it is especially suited to heavy cover.
The breed is believed to have originated in France.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 18-20 inches (male), 17-19 inches (female) and weight as 70-85 pounds (male), 55-70 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Cocker Spaniel

job.text: The Cocker Spaniel was developed to find game birds in dense cover, flush them, and bring the fallen bird back.

breeds.home: In a house, that bird work can look like a dog who wants to sniff through grass and carry things back to a person. A walk in cover, and a retrieve at the end, is the household version of the old hunting job.

facts.text: The Cocker uses its nose to find birds such as grouse or pheasant in dense bushes and high grass.
The dog flushes the birds so a hunter can shoot, then brings the fallen bird back.
The name cocker comes from a special skill on woodcock.
Spaniels are believed to have begun in Spain, and the words Spain and spaniel are closely related.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 14.5-15.5 inches (male), 13.5-14.5 inches (female) and weight as 25-30 pounds (male), 20-25 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Collie

job.text: The Collie was developed as a drover, guiding sheep and cattle to market in Scotland and northern England.

breeds.home: At home, that droving work can look like a dog who wants to keep a group moving together. A walk where the dog can circle and stay with the household gives the old market job a small version.

facts.text: Collies were mostly used as drovers, guiding sheep and cows to market.
They have worked as herding dogs in Scotland and northern England for hundreds of years.
Victoria popularized the local herding breed during her long stays at Balmoral Castle in the Scottish Highlands.
There are two varieties of Collie, rough and smooth.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24-26 inches (male), 22-24 inches (female) and weight as 60-75 pounds (male), 50-65 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Coton de Tulear

job.text: The Coton de Tulear was kept as a lapdog by nobles on Madagascar.

breeds.home: In a house, that lapdog role looks like a dog who wants to be close, often in someone's lap. Time with people, and a place nearby, is the household version of the old companion job.

facts.text: The breed is named for the seaport town of Tulear and was once the preferred lapdog of Madagascar's nobles.
On Madagascar, the world's fourth largest island, Cotons were once the pet favored by tribal nobles.
The dog's French name endured because French is still widely spoken by Malagasy elites.
In its home country, the breed has been shown on a postage stamp.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10-11 inches (male), 9-10 inches (female) and weight as 9-15 pounds (male), 8-13 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Curly-Coated Retriever

job.text: The Curly-Coated Retriever was developed as a water dog to retrieve game for hunters using rifles.

breeds.home: At home, that retrieving work can look like a dog who wants to swim and bring things back. A fetch game and time in the water give the old gundog job a place off the marsh.

facts.text: The breed was developed in the 1800s from crosses of older water dogs.
Irish Water Spaniels and Poodles may be part of that mix.
Retrievers came along only after wing shooting with rifles became practical, sometime in the late 1700s.
By 1860, Curlies were a popular sight at England's first dog shows.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25-27 inches (male), 23-25 inches (female) and weight as 60-95 pounds.

breeds.name: Dachshund

job.text: The Dachshund was developed in Germany to dig into a badger's den and hunt the badger.

breeds.home: In a house, that den work can look like a dog who wants to dig and follow a scent into tight spaces. A place to dig outdoors, and a chance to sniff along the ground, gives the badger job a tame outlet.

facts.text: The name Dachshund means badger dog in German.
The dog was bred to dig into a badger's den and hunt the animal inside.
Badger dogs go back to the 1400s, and this breed has been around since the 1600s.
Dachshunds are bred in smooth, long, and wirehaired coats, and in standard and miniature sizes.
The AKC page for the Standard variety lists height as 8-9 inches (standard), 5-6 inches (miniature) and weight as 16-32 pounds (standard), 11 pounds & under (miniature).

breeds.name: Dalmatian

job.text: The Dalmatian was bred to trot beside horse-drawn coaches and to watch the horses and rig when they were left alone.

breeds.home: At home, that coach-dog work can look like a dog who wants to run alongside people and stay near the household's comings and goings. A chance to trot with a person, and a place to keep watch, fits the old carriage job.

facts.text: Dalmatians were bred to trot beside horse-drawn coaches and to watch the horses and rig when no one else was there.
The dogs traveled with Romani caravans on their wanderings around Europe.
When horses pulled fire engines, Dalmatians began a long association with firefighters.
Puppies of this breed are born with no spots.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 19-24 inches and weight as 45-70 pounds.

breeds.name: Dandie Dinmont Terrier

job.text: The Dandie Dinmont was a rough native terrier that took its name from a farmer in Sir Walter Scott's novel Guy Mannering.

breeds.home: In a house, that terrier background can look like a dog who wants to investigate and then settle with its people. A walk with time to sniff, and a place in the household, gives the old terrier life a daily shape.

facts.text: In Sir Walter Scott's 1815 novel Guy Mannering, a farmer named Dandie Dinmont keeps a pack of pepper and mustard terriers.
Scott based that character on a real breeder of these dogs.
While the novel was popular, the dogs became known as Dandie Dinmont's terriers.
The terrier that became the Dandie Dinmont first appears in written history about 1700.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 8-11 inches and weight as 18-24 pounds.

breeds.name: Danish-Swedish Farmdog

job.text: The Danish-Swedish Farmdog was an all-purpose farm dog, used as a ratter, herder, hunting dog, watchdog, and companion.

breeds.home: At home, that farm mix can look like a dog who wants to keep an eye on the household, check a small rustle, and stay in the middle of family life. A home with a bit of work to do, and people to follow, fits the old farm day.

facts.text: The dog was originally known as the Danish Pincher and was a regular part of Danish farm life.
Everyday work included ratting, herding livestock, hunting, watching, and keeping the family company.
The Danish and Swedish kennel clubs' effort to bring the breed back produced the first breed standard in 1987.
In 1998 a dog was imported to the United States to start the first official breeding program there.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 12.5-14.5 inches and weight as 15-20 pounds.

breeds.name: Doberman Pinscher

job.text: The Doberman Pinscher was bred by the tax collector Louis Dobermann as a protection dog to go with him on his rounds.

breeds.home: In a house, that accompanying work can look like a dog who wants to stay with its person and notice what is happening around them. A walk together, and a clear place in the household, is the home version of going along on the rounds.

facts.text: In the 1890s, the German tax collector Louis Dobermann bred a protection dog to accompany him on his rounds.
The Rottweiler, Greyhound, Manchester Terrier, and Miniature Pinscher are mentioned as possible parts of the mix.
The breed began in Apolda, in Thueringen, Germany, around 1890.
The original dog was known as the Tax Collector's Dog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 26-28 inches (male), 24-26 inches (female) and weight as 75-100 pounds (male), 60-90 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Dogo Argentino

job.text: The Dogo Argentino was developed in Argentina to hunt big game and to live as a family companion.

breeds.home: At home, that combination can look like a dog who wants a person to work with and a household to belong to. A long outing with a job to do, then a quiet return home, echoes the work the breed was made for.

facts.text: Brothers Antonio and Augustin Nores Martinez, teenagers in the 1920s, set out to create a big-game hunter that could also be a family companion.
Their foundation dog was the Cordoba Fighting Dog, now extinct, crossed over 20 years with nine other breeds.
In Argentina the breed is used to hunt big game, mainly boar and mountain lion.
The breed comes from the province of Cordoba, in the central Mediterranean region.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24-26.5 inches (male), 24-25.5 inches (female) and weight as 80-100 pounds.

breeds.name: Dogue de Bordeaux

job.text: The Dogue de Bordeaux worked as a cattle drover, a draft dog, and a guardian.

breeds.home: In a house, that work can look like a dog who wants to stay with the household and keep track of who belongs there. A walk with a person, and a settled place at home, gives the old drover and guardian roles a quieter day.

facts.text: The Dogue de Bordeaux is called the oldest French dog breed, and it was around before France was France.
Over a long history the breed worked as a cattle drover, a draft dog, and a guardian.
In ancient times, when France was Gaul and a Roman province, these dogs were developed as war dogs and gladiators.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23.27 inches (male), 23-26 inches (female) and weight as 110 pounds & up (male), 99 pounds & up (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 2008 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: English Cocker Spaniel

job.text: The English Cocker Spaniel was bred as a smaller spaniel to hunt woodcock.

breeds.home: At home, that woodcock work can look like a dog who wants to hunt through brush and stay close enough for a person to follow. A walk in grass and cover, with a retrieve at the end, is the home version of the old bird job.

facts.text: In the late 1800s, spaniels were split into springers and cockers, and the cockers were the smaller dogs bred to hunt woodcock.
Into the early 20th century, English Cockers and Springer Spaniels were told apart by height alone.
The American Kennel Club recognized the English Cocker Spaniel as a separate breed in 1946.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 16-17 inches (male), 15-16 inches (female) and weight as 28-34 pounds (male), 26-32 pounds (female).

breeds.name: English Foxhound

job.text: The English Foxhound was developed to hunt fox in a pack, with mounted hunters following.

breeds.home: In a house, that pack-hunting work can look like a dog who wants to run with company and follow a scent for a long time. A long outing with other dogs, or a person who keeps moving, gives the foxhound job somewhere to go.

facts.text: Masters of hounds built the breed by crossing big stag-hunting hounds, for nose and endurance, with leggy coursing hounds, for speed and agility.
The traditional British foxhunt, with packs of hounds and mounted hunters, began in the 1600s.
In the 1700s, American sportsmen including George Washington used the English Foxhound in creating the American Foxhound.
These hounds have been used for foxhunting in the English style of riding to hounds.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24 inches and weight as 60-75 pounds.

breeds.name: English Setter

job.text: The English Setter was bred on English country estates, from spaniels and pointers, to hunt birds.

breeds.home: At home, that bird-dog work can look like a dog who wants to range out, stop on a scent, and then come back to a person. A long walk in open ground gives the old setter job a place to happen.

facts.text: More than 400 years ago, English Setters were already trained bird dogs in England.
They were first bred on the estates of English country gentlemen, who crossed older spaniels and pointers.
One line, the Laverac setters, was bred as companions and show dogs, and the Llewellin line was used mainly as gundogs.
English Setters had their first show at Newcastle-On-Tyne on January 28, 1859.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25-27 inches (male), 23-25 inches (female) and weight as 65-80 pounds (male), 45-55 pounds (female).

breeds.name: English Springer Spaniel

job.text: The English Springer Spaniel was bred to find game birds, spring them from cover, and retrieve the bird.

breeds.home: In a house, that spaniel work can look like a dog who wants to quarter through grass and bring something back. A walk in rough cover, and a retrieve for a person, is the household version of the old bird job.

facts.text: Springers first worked game birds alongside hunters who used nets and falcons.
After the hunting rifle arrived in the 17th century, Springers became gundogs.
The name Springer comes from flushing, or springing, birds from their cover.
In 1902 the Kennel Club of England recognized the English Springer as a breed separate from English Cockers.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 20 inches (male), 19 inches (female) and weight as 50 pounds (male), 40 pounds (female).

breeds.name: English Toy Spaniel

job.text: The English Toy Spaniel was kept as a small companion, later bred into a smaller, flatter-faced toy spaniel.

breeds.home: At home, that companion role looks like a dog who wants to be near people and settle close by. A lap and a place in the family's rooms is the household version of that old companion life.

facts.text: The toy spaniels of Charles I and Charles II became symbols of the House of Stuart.
In Victorian times those older toy spaniels were refined into a smaller, flatter-faced breed.
The breed's origins are placed in the East, namely Japan.
A professor and physician to Queen Elizabeth called these dogs the Spaniell Gentle, otherwise the Comforter.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 9-10 inches and weight as 8-14 pounds.

breeds.name: Entlebucher Mountain Dog

job.text: The Entlebucher Mountain Dog was developed to drive cattle up to high mountain pastures for the summer and bring them back to the valley for winter.

breeds.home: In a house, that cattle work can look like a dog who wants to keep a group together and move with them. A walk where the dog can follow and gather the household gives the mountain droving job a small version.

facts.text: The breed is named for the valley of Entlebuch, where it began.
Its main task was to drive cattle to high pastures in summer, watch them while they grazed, and bring them back down for winter.
On the path, the dog's herding job was to keep the cows together while crossing rocky, uneven Alpine ground.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 17.5-20.5 inches (male), 16.5-19.5 inches (female) and weight as 50-65 pounds (male), 40-55 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 2011 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Field Spaniel

job.text: The Field Spaniel was developed as a hunting spaniel to flush game birds.

breeds.home: At home, that flushing work can look like a dog who wants to search through cover and stay in touch with a person. A walk in grass and brush gives the old gundog job somewhere to go.

facts.text: In the early 1800s, Field Spaniels were able, dependable hunting dogs.
After dog shows arrived around mid-century, breeders pushed the long, low shape so far that the dog was no longer useful as a gundog.
In the late 1960s, fanciers rebuilt the Field Spaniel along its original working lines.
Well into the 1800s, the British spaniels used to flush game birds were not yet divided into separate breeds.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 18 inches (male), 17 inches (female) and weight as 35-50 pounds.

breeds.name: Finnish Lapphund

job.text: The Finnish Lapphund was developed by the Sami people, first to hunt reindeer and later to herd them.

breeds.home: In a house, that herding work can look like a dog who wants to keep the household together and move them along. A walk with a group, and a person to work with, gives the reindeer job a smaller shape.

facts.text: The semi-nomadic Sami people of Lapland, in the far north of Scandinavia, created the Lapphund in ancient times.
The dogs were first used to hunt reindeer, and after the Sami settled they switched to herding reindeer.
The breed is also known as the Lapinkoira.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 18-21 inches (male), 16-19 inches (female) and weight as 33-53 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 2011 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Finnish Spitz

job.text: The Finnish Spitz was used as an all-purpose hunter that finds treed birds and holds them with its bark until a person arrives.

breeds.home: At home, that bird-dog work can look like a dog who barks to point something out and wants a person to come see. A walk in the woods, with time to look up into the trees, gives the old hunting style a place to happen.

facts.text: It is assumed that migrants from central Russia brought spitz-type dogs when they arrived in what is now Finland some 3,000 years ago.
For centuries these dogs were all-purpose hunters of mammals and game birds.
The dog barks in a rapid yodel and wags its tail slowly at the bird.
In Finland, the country's most popular breed is called the Suomenpystykorva.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 17.5-20 inches (male), 15.5-18 inches (female) and weight as 25-33 pounds (male), 20-28 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Flat-Coated Retriever

job.text: The Flat-Coated Retriever was developed to mark fallen waterfowl and swim out to bring the bird back.

breeds.home: In a house, that retrieving work can look like a dog who wants to fetch, swim, and work closely with a person. A game of fetch and time near water give the lake-hunting job a place at home.

facts.text: The Flat-Coat is one of the retrievers that bring back downed waterfowl.
The dog marks where a duck falls, swims a straight line to it, and carries the bird gently.
The Flat-Coat came out of the same Labrador family as the Labrador Retriever.
H. R. Cooke kept the breed for more than 70 years at his Riverside kennel.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23-24.5 inches (male), 22-23.5 inches (female) and weight as 60-70 pounds.

breeds.name: French Bulldog

job.text: The French Bulldog was bred down from the Bulldog by lacemakers in Nottingham to keep as a lapdog.

breeds.home: At home, that lapdog role looks like a dog who wants to stay close and share the room with people. A place on the couch and a person to follow from room to room is the home version of the lacemaker's companion.

facts.text: Lacemakers bred the Bulldog down to a smaller size to keep as a lapdog.
When the Industrial Revolution took the lacemakers to France, they brought the dogs with them.
One ancestor is the English Bulldog, most likely of the toy variety.
The breed was first called the Boule-Dog Francais.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 11-13 inches and weight as under 28 pounds.

breeds.name: German Pinscher

job.text: The German Pinscher originally made its living as a ratter, seizing and nipping vermin.

breeds.home: In a house, that ratting work can look like a dog who notices small movement and wants to investigate it. A home where the dog can patrol and then settle with the family gives the old vermin job a tame shape.

facts.text: The word pinscher appears to come from the French word pincer, meaning to seize or to nip.
Seizing and nipping are how the breed first earned its keep, by killing rats.
The German Pinscher is a parent of the Miniature Pinscher and the Doberman.
The German Pinscher is known for its ability to hunt vermin.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 17-20 inches and weight as 25-45 pounds.

breeds.name: German Shepherd Dog

job.text: The German Shepherd Dog was developed in Germany from older herding and farm dogs.

breeds.home: At home, that herding background can look like a dog who wants a person to work with and a task to do. A walk with a purpose, and a household to stay with, gives the old farm work a modern shape.

facts.text: Captain Max von Stephanitz, a German cavalry officer, developed the breed in the late 19th century.
The breed was made through crosses of older farming and herding dogs of continental Europe.
The breed descends from German herding dogs that, until the late 19th century, varied from district to district.
Rin-Tin-Tin and Strongheart helped make the breed popular in the United States in the early 1900s.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24-26 inches (male), 22-24 inches (female) and weight as 65-90 pounds (male), 50-70 pounds (female).
