breeds.name: German Shorthaired Pointer

job.text: The German Shorthaired Pointer was developed as an all-purpose gundog that could hunt on land and in water.

breeds.home: In a house, that gundog work can look like a dog who wants to search, swim, and stay in close touch with a person. A long outing on land or near water, with a retrieve, gives the hunting job a place to go.

facts.text: German hunters crossed various breeds for generations and had this versatile gundog by the 1800s.
A water-repellent coat lets the breed work in water as well as on land.
The breed is used to hunt many kinds of game.
In the late 19th and early 20th centuries, breeders selected the dog for biddability, and later worked on stance, style, and nose.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23-25 inches (male), 21-23 inches (female) and weight as 55-70 pounds (male), 45-60 pounds (female).

breeds.name: German Wirehaired Pointer

job.text: The German Wirehaired Pointer was developed as an all-purpose gundog for both land and water.

breeds.home: At home, that utility work can look like a dog who wants to hunt, swim, and keep working with a person. A long walk and time in the water give the all-purpose gundog job somewhere to go.

facts.text: Early wirehaired pointers combined the Griffon, Stichelhaar, Pudelpointer, and German Shorthair.
The Pudelpointer in that mix was a cross between a Poodle and an English Pointer.
The breed works as well on land as in water, helped by its coat.
These dogs were first imported to North America in the 1920s.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24-26 inches (male), minimum 22 inches (female) and weight as 50-70 pounds.

breeds.name: Giant Schnauzer

job.text: The Giant Schnauzer was developed to drive cattle from farm to market and to guard farms, shops, and inns.

breeds.home: In a house, that work can look like a dog who wants to move along with people and keep an eye on the home. A walk with a purpose, and a household to watch, gives the cattle-driving and guarding jobs a daily place.

facts.text: Development of the breed took place in the Bavarian Alps in the middle of the 1800s.
Bred up from the Standard Schnauzer, the dogs were used to drive cattle from farm to market.
They also guarded for farmers, merchants, and innkeepers.
After railroads ended the cattle drives, Giants were used as police and military dogs in Europe.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25.5-27.5 inches (male), 23.5-25.5 inches (female) and weight as 75-95 pounds (male), 55-80 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Glen of Imaal Terrier

job.text: The Glen of Imaal Terrier was developed to hunt badgers and to do odd jobs around the farm.

breeds.home: At home, that work can look like a dog who wants to dig, investigate, and stay busy at a task. A chance to sniff and dig, and a household to follow, gives the old farm terrier day a smaller shape.

facts.text: The breed comes from the remote, rocky Glen of Imaal in County Wicklow.
Glens were developed as badger hunters and also did odd jobs around the farm.
Some accounts say they ran a kitchen wheel that turned meat over an open fire, which earned the nickname Turnspit Dog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 12.5-14 inches and weight as 32-40 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 2004 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Golden Retriever

job.text: The Golden Retriever was developed in the Scottish Highlands as a hunting dog for rainy weather and rugged ground.

breeds.home: In a house, that retrieving work can look like a dog who wants to carry things, swim, and stay close to a person. A game of fetch and time outdoors give the hunting job a place at home.

facts.text: Dudley Marjoribanks, the first Lord Tweedmouth, developed the breed in the Scottish Highlands.
He crossed a Yellow Retriever with the Tweed Water Spaniel, a breed that is now extinct.
Bloodhound and Irish Setter also went into the mix.
Goldens were first shown in England at the Crystal Palace show in 1908, listed as Flat Coats (Golden).
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23-24 inches (male), 21.5-22.5 inches (female) and weight as 65-75 pounds (male), 55-65 pounds (female).

atts.text: American Temperament Test Society. Golden Retrievers: 85.9% pass rate, 836 dogs.
atts.note: A pass rate is a number, not a verdict. You decide what it means.

breeds.name: Gordon Setter

job.text: The Gordon Setter was developed in Scotland as a large bird dog for hard country.

breeds.home: At home, that bird-dog work can look like a dog who wants to range through rough ground and then come back to a person. A long walk in open country gives the setter job somewhere to happen.

facts.text: Scots huntsmen bred hounds and collys into setter lines and produced a large bird dog for difficult conditions.
Alexander, Fourth Duke of Gordon, kept these dogs at Castle Gordon.
By the early 1800s the duke's kennel was producing setters recognizable as the breed that bears his name.
The Gordon Setter's lineage is dated to 1620.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24-27 inches (male), 23-26 inches (female) and weight as 55-80 pounds (male), 45-70 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Grand Basset Griffon Vendéen

job.text: The Grand Basset Griffon Vendéen was developed as a hound for dense, thorny, rocky country, at a pace hunters on foot could follow.

breeds.home: In a house, that hunting work can look like a dog who wants to follow a scent through rough cover and keep a pace a person can share. A long walk on foot, with time to trail, gives the old hound job a place to go.

facts.text: Griffon Vendéen hounds developed over more than 400 years into the coated French hounds known today.
The dense, thorny, rocky region of the Vendeé called for a hardy dog whose coat could resist brambles.
Hunters who had no horses needed a slower hound so they could keep up on foot.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 15.5-18 inches and weight as 40-45 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 2018 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Great Dane

job.text: The Great Dane was used by German nobles to hunt wild boar, and later to protect the home.

breeds.home: At home, that later role looks like a dog who stays with the household and notices who comes to the door. A place in the home, and a person to accompany, is the indoor version of the old protector's job.

facts.text: German nobles used Danes to hunt wild boar.
Later, Danes became known as protectors of home and family.
In Germany the breed is called the Deutsche Dog, or German dog.
The English name comes from the French grand Danois, meaning big Danish.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 30-32 inches (male), 28-30 inches (female) and weight as 140-175 pounds (male), 110-140 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Great Pyrenees

job.text: The Great Pyrenees was bred to watch flocks in the Pyrenees Mountains and to deter wolves, bears, and livestock rustlers.

breeds.home: In a house, that flock-watching work can look like a dog who wants a wide view of the household and the yard. A place to lie and watch, and a family to stay with, is the home version of sitting with the sheep.

facts.text: The breed was bred to work with shepherds and herding dogs in the Pyrenees, the mountains between France and Spain.
The job was to watch the flock and deter wolves, bears, and livestock rustlers.
Remains of the breed have been found in fossil deposits from the Bronze Age.
The Pyrenees was taken up as a French court dog in the 17th century.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 27-32 inches (male), 25-29 inches (female) and weight as 100 pounds & up (male), 85 pounds & up (female).

breeds.name: Greater Swiss Mountain Dog

job.text: The Greater Swiss Mountain Dog was developed as a farm and draft dog, hauling meat and dairy to market in dogcarts.

breeds.home: At home, that draft work can look like a dog who wants to pull and to have a task around the home. A harness walk gives the old cart job a small version.

facts.text: The breed descends from dogs brought over the Alps by Julius Caesar's legions.
The Swiss used those mastiff-type dogs when breeding their Alpine mountain dogs, the Sennenhund.
In mountain passes they hauled loads of meat and dairy to market in dogcarts.
The Greater Swiss is closely related to the Bernese Mountain Dog and is part of the background of the Saint Bernard and the Rottweiler.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25.5-28.5 inches (male), 23.7-27 inches (female) and weight as 115-140 pounds (male), 85-110 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Greyhound

job.text: The Greyhound was developed in Egypt to find, chase, and catch fast desert wildlife.

breeds.home: In a house, that coursing work can look like a dog who wants a short, fast run and then a long rest. A fenced place to sprint, followed by a quiet couch, is the home version of the desert chase.

facts.text: The Greyhound's story begins in Egypt some 5,000 years ago.
The pharaohs' hounds were made to find, chase, catch, and bring down the fast wildlife of Egypt's deserts.
Among dog breeds, the Greyhound is the fastest.
One theory traces the name to Graius, meaning Grecian.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 28-30 inches (male), 27-28 inches (female) and weight as 65-70 pounds (male), 60-65 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Harrier

job.text: The Harrier was bred to hunt hare in packs.

breeds.home: At home, that hare-hunting work can look like a dog who wants to follow a scent with company and keep going. A long walk, with time to trail, gives the pack-hound job somewhere to go.

facts.text: The breed was bred to hunt hare, and the name is based on the word hare.
The first pack in England was the Penistone, established by Sir Elias de Midhope in 1260.
The Harrier of today is generally believed to be a smaller Foxhound, bred down by selection.
The name is thought to come from the Norman word harier, for Saxon hounds.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 19-21 inches and weight as 45-60 pounds.

breeds.name: Havanese

job.text: The Havanese was kept as a companion dog by the aristocrats and merchants of Havana.

breeds.home: In a house, that companion role looks like a dog who wants to be with people and stay close through the day. A lap and a share of the household routine is the home version of the old pet's life.

facts.text: European traders brought the Havanese to Cuba in the 1600s, and the dogs became pets of Havana's aristocrats and wealthy merchants.
The breed was once called the Havana Silk Dog or the Spanish Silk Poodle.
The Havanese comes from the Bichon family and shares that family's ancestor, the Tenerife.
The Bichon Frise and the Maltese are among the breeds it claims.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 8.5-11.5 inches and weight as 7-13 pounds.

breeds.name: Ibizan Hound

job.text: The Ibizan Hound was used in packs to hunt rabbits on the island of Ibiza.

breeds.home: At home, that rabbit hunting can look like a dog who wants to course and follow a moving scent. A long chance to run gives the island hunting job somewhere to go.

facts.text: About 3,000 years ago, Phoenician traders brought Egyptian hounds to the rocky island.
Islanders used packs of these hounds to hunt rabbits.
On rugged Ibiza, food was scarce, and chasing rabbits was closer to a meal than to sport.
Ibizan Hound history is traced to about 3400 BC.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23.5-27.5 inches (male), 22.5-26 inches (female) and weight as 50 pounds (male), 45 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Icelandic Sheepdog

job.text: The Icelandic Sheepdog was developed to herd sheep and round up ponies.

breeds.home: In a house, that herding work can look like a dog who wants to keep the family together and move them along from room to room.

facts.text: Among what they brought from Norway were spitz-type dogs that Icelanders used for herding sheep and rounding up ponies.
About 1,100 years ago, Norse settlers crossed the Norwegian Sea to Iceland.
The breed is Iceland's only native dog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 18 inches (male), 16.5 inches (female) and weight as 30 pounds (male), 25 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 2010 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Irish Red and White Setter

job.text: The Irish Red and White Setter was developed to creep close to game birds and hold a set so a hunter could net them.

breeds.home: In a house, that setting work can look like a dog who goes still when a scent is worth reporting, and who likes a long, careful search.

facts.text: Before the all-red Irish Setter, the red and white dog was a fixture of Ireland's hills and bogs since at least the 1600s.
Setters crawled toward game birds, froze in a setting position, and signaled with the tail until a hunter threw a net.
When nets gave way to firearms, setter lines adapted that crouching style of hunting.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24.5-26 inches (male), 22.5-24 inches (female) and weight as 42-60 pounds (male), 35-50 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 2009 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Irish Setter

job.text: The Irish Setter was developed to find game birds by scent and set on its belly for the hunter.

breeds.home: In a house, that bird-dog work can look like a dog who air-scents, then drops low and holds still when a smell is worth showing.

facts.text: A setter shows the hunter it has found birds by setting down on its belly.
Before guns, setters worked with trained falcons and with hunters who used nets.
The Irish Setter is believed to come from a mix of English Setter, spaniel, pointer, and Gordon Setter.
Solid red Irish Setters first appeared in Ireland in the 19th century.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 27 inches (male), 25 inches (female) and weight as 70 pounds (male), 60 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Irish Terrier

job.text: The Irish Terrier was developed as an all-purpose farm dog, to catch rats and also to watch, guard, and hunt.

breeds.home: In a house, that farm work can look like a dog who checks the yard, notices who comes and goes, and is ready to chase anything that scurries.

facts.text: For hundreds of years the Irish Terrier was a farm dog in rural Ireland, and a ratter.
These dogs also worked as watchdogs, flock and family guardians, and hunting companions on land and lake.
In World War I the Irish Terrier was used as a messenger and sentinel.
The first record of the breed being shown as a recognized breed dates to 1875 in Glasgow, Scotland.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 18 inches and weight as 27 pounds (male), 25 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Irish Water Spaniel

job.text: The Irish Water Spaniel was developed to retrieve waterfowl from the waterways of southern Ireland.

breeds.home: In a house, that water work can look like a dog who wants to swim, fetch from the water, and carry things back.

facts.text: By the late Middle Ages, rat-tailed spaniels were working the waterways of southern Ireland.
Curly-coated Irish water dogs fitting this description appear in Renaissance writings.
In the 1830s, sportsman Justin McCarthy set the breed's type with his dog Boatswain.
The breed gained a reputation on both sides of the Atlantic as a waterfowl retriever.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 22-24 inches (male), 21-23 inches (female) and weight as 55-68 pounds (male), 45-58 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Irish Wolfhound

job.text: The Irish Wolfhound was developed to hunt big game and later to hunt the wolves of Ireland.

breeds.home: In a house, that hunting work can look like a dog who wants a long run and a trail to follow, then a quiet place to rest.

facts.text: The breed was created by breeding Middle Eastern hounds to large dogs of Britain.
By about the 15th century, when wolves were overrunning Ireland, these big-game hunters began to specialize on wolves.
By the late 1700s the wolves of Ireland had been hunted out, and the dogs nearly disappeared with the job.
In 391 AD the Irish Wolfhound was known in Rome, and the Roman consul Quintus Aurelius wrote the first authentic mention of it.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 32 inches minimum (male), 30 inches minimum (female) and weight as 120 pounds (male), 105 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Italian Greyhound

job.text: The Italian Greyhound was developed as a small companion.

breeds.home: In a house, that companion role can look like a dog who stays near the family.

facts.text: Archaeological evidence suggests these dogs were bred as noble companions about 2,000 years ago, at the height of Roman power in the Mediterranean.
The breed came into its own in Renaissance Italy, where miniature versions of popular breeds were a fad among the wealthy.
It is the smallest of the gazehounds, or sighthounds.
Italian Greyhounds were nearly wiped out in World War II, and American breeders far from the war kept the breed alive.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 13-15 inches and weight as 7-14 pounds.

breeds.name: Japanese Chin

job.text: The Japanese Chin was developed as a companion cultivated by Japanese nobles.

breeds.home: In a house, that companion role can look like a dog who prefers to stay close, watch the room, and share quiet daily life.

facts.text: Origin tales credit Buddhist monks, Chinese emperors, or European merchants with bringing the Chin to Japan somewhere between 500 and 1,000 years ago.
Japanese nobles are the people who cultivated the breed as it is known today.
The Chin was unknown in the West until 1854, when Japan reopened for trade after 200 years of isolation.
The breed is described as coming from the lapdogs of Chinese aristocracy.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 8-11 inches and weight as 7-11 pounds.

breeds.name: Keeshond

job.text: The Keeshond was developed as a guard and companion on Dutch barges.

breeds.home: In a house, that barge-dog work can look like a dog who stays with the family, notices visitors, and wants to be in the middle of household comings and goings.

facts.text: The Keeshond was a barge dog kept as a guard and companion on Dutch vessels along the waterways of the Low Countries.
In the 18th century the breed was a symbol of the Dutch Patriots Party in its opposition to the House of Orange.
The name may refer to a Patriot mascot dog called Kees, or to two Patriot leaders nicknamed Kees.
The breed's origin is described as Arctic or possibly sub-Arctic.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 18 inches (male), 17 inches (female) and weight as 35-45 pounds.

breeds.name: Kerry Blue Terrier

job.text: The Kerry Blue Terrier was developed as an all-around farm dog.

breeds.home: In a house, that farm work can look like a dog who wants a task, keeps an eye on the household, and is ready to follow the family from one job to the next.

facts.text: Kerries were hardworking all-around farm dogs.
The breed was a mascot for patriots in the struggle for Irish independence.
One account says the peasantry of Ireland developed the Kerry as an answer to nobility who used Irish Wolfhounds.
Kerry Blues are born black, and the coat fades to a solid slate gray by 18 months.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 18-19.5 inches (male), 17.5-19 inches (female) and weight as 33-40 pounds (male), females weigh proportionately less than males.

breeds.name: Komondor

job.text: The Komondor was developed to guard sheep at pasture and drive off wolves and other predators.

breeds.home: In a house, that guarding work can look like a dog who stays with the family, watches the edge of the yard, and takes time to decide who belongs.

facts.text: The Komondor guards sheep at pasture and is expected to run off wolves and other predators.
The cords protect the dog from extreme weather and from sharp-toothed predators.
The breed is one of three working dogs native for ten centuries to Hungary's sheep and cattle country.
The Komondor is descended from Tibetan dogs and was brought to Hungary a thousand years ago by nomadic Magyars.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 27.5 minimum inches (male), 25.5 minimum inches (female) and weight as 100 pounds or more (male), 80 pounds or more (female).

breeds.name: Kuvasz

job.text: The Kuvasz was developed to guard livestock, watching the flock and facing wolves or rustlers.

breeds.home: In a house, that guardian work can look like a dog who keeps a long watch on the family and the yard, and who pays attention when a stranger is at the edge of the property.

facts.text: The Kuvasz came to Hungary in the Middle Ages, and the line is thought to go back to ancient Turkey and Tibet.
As livestock guardians they watched the flock for days and were expected to face wolves or armed rustlers.
King Matthais I is said to have trusted his Kuvs more than his palace guards.
In the fifteenth century the Kuvasz was kept at the court of King Matthias, who claimed to trust only his Kuvasz dogs.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 28-30 inches (male), 26-28 inches (female) and weight as 100-115 pounds (male), 70-90 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Labrador Retriever

job.text: The Labrador Retriever was developed as a water dog to retrieve ducks and help fishermen.

breeds.home: In a house, that retrieving work can look like a dog who wants to carry things, fetch from the water, and stay busy alongside the family.

facts.text: The Labrador is the traditional water dog of Newfoundland, long used as a duck retriever and a fisherman's mate.
Labs worked beside fishermen and hunters, helping them catch fish and retrieve game.
In the early 19th century, Lord Malmsbury bought several in Canada and brought them to Britain because of their retrieving instinct.
Despite the name, the Labrador Retriever comes from Newfoundland, not from Labrador.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 22.5-24.5 inches (male), 21.5-23.5 inches (female) and weight as 65-80 pounds (male), 55-70 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Lagotto Romagnolo

job.text: The Lagotto Romagnolo was developed to retrieve waterfowl in the marshes, and later to find truffles by scent.

breeds.home: In a house, that nose work can look like a dog who wants to search, sniff along the ground, and bring back what it finds.

facts.text: Lagotti go back to at least Renaissance Italy, where they were bred as waterfowl retrievers in the marshlands of Ravenna.
The name is tied to water: Lago is Italian for lake.
For many years they have been used in the Italian countryside to sniff out truffles.
The Lagotto is the only purebred dog recognized as a specialized truffle searcher.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 17-19 inches (male), 16-18 inches (female) and weight as 28.5-35 pounds (male), 24-31 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Lakeland Terrier

job.text: The Lakeland Terrier was developed to work in small packs and clear foxes from sheep farms in the Lake District.

breeds.home: In a house, that terrier work can look like a dog who wants to investigate holes and edges, and who is happiest with a real job outdoors.

facts.text: Lakelands are among the oldest of Britain's terriers, and the name comes from the Lake District in northern England.
Farmers there used small packs of dogs to clear foxes that raided sheepfolds.
The Lakeland was first and foremost a workingman's working terrier.
The breed has also been called the Patterdale, Fell, Cumberland, and Westmoreland terrier.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 14.5-15 inches (male), slightly smaller (female) and weight as 17 pounds (male), slightly smaller (female).

breeds.name: Lancashire Heeler

job.text: The Lancashire Heeler was developed to herd cattle, catch rats, and help drive stock to market.

breeds.home: In a house, that work can look like a dog who follows at the heels, wants to move people along, and notices small movement around the yard.

facts.text: A type of Welsh Corgi is thought to have driven stock from northern Wales to the Lancashire market.
A small black and tan dog known as the butchers' dog was common in the Ormskirk area of West Lancashire.
Possible ancestors include the Corgi and the Manchester Terrier.
The breed was once a cattle herder and a ratter.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10-12 inches and weight as 9-17 pounds.

breeds.name: Leonberger

job.text: The Leonberger was developed as a large companion dog.

breeds.home: In a house, that companion role can look like a dog who wants to be near the family and share the room with them.

facts.text: Heinrich Essig, a mid-19th-century politician and entrepreneur of Leonberg, Germany, developed the breed first as a companion.
He used Saint Bernards and Newfoundlands, among other large working breeds.
His clients included Napoleon III, Russia's Tsar Alexander II, and the Prince of Wales, later King Edward VII.
Legend says Heinrich Essig wanted a dog that resembled the lion on the town crest.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 28-31.5 inches (male), 25.5-29.5 inches (female) and weight as 110-170 pounds (male), 90-140 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Lhasa Apso

job.text: The Lhasa Apso was developed as a sentinel for palaces and Buddhist monasteries in the Himalayas.

breeds.home: In a house, that sentinel work can look like a dog who notices sounds at the door and lets the household know someone is there.

facts.text: This old breed served as a sentinel at palaces and Buddhist monasteries high in the Himalayan Mountains.
In the late 1940s, dogs bred and given by the Fourteenth Dalai Lama helped establish the breed in America.
The original name was Abso Seng Kye, the Bark Lion Sentinel Dog.
Suydam Cutting, a naturalist and traveler, is credited with establishing the Lhasa in America.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10-11 inches (male), slightly smaller (female) and weight as 12-18 pounds.

breeds.name: Löwchen

job.text: The Löwchen was developed as a companion for noble households.

breeds.home: In a house, that companion role can look like a dog who stays close to people and likes to be included in the day's quiet routines.

facts.text: The name is German, but historians do not agree on a birthplace, and since the Middle Ages the breed was popular with noblewomen in France, Italy, Holland, Spain, Russia, and Germany.
The Löwchen comes from the same ancient line as the Bichon Frise and the Maltese.
Renaissance art in several countries shows that the look has held for at least 500 years.
The breed may be from Germany, though for many years a Mediterranean origin was the belief.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 12-14 inches and weight as 15 pounds.

breeds.name: Maltese

job.text: The Maltese was developed as a small lapdog traded from Malta around the ancient world.

breeds.home: In a house, that companion role can look like a dog who wants to be near people and is content to share a chair or a lap.

facts.text: Seafaring traders bartered a little white lapdog for export around the ancient world.
For three thousand years the Maltese has been a favored pet of nobles and notables.
People tied to Maltese history and legend include Aristotle, St. Paul the Apostle, Mary Queen of Scots, and Napoleon.
The Greeks erected tombs to their Maltese.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 7-9 inches and weight as under 7 pounds.

breeds.name: Manchester Terrier (Standard)

job.text: The Manchester Terrier was developed to hunt rabbits and to catch rats.

breeds.home: In a house, that work can look like a dog who notices small movement, wants to chase a scurry, and likes a fast run in an open space.

facts.text: In the mid-1800s, local mill workers hunted rabbits with small hounds and set terriers on rats.
Breeders crossed a ratter called the Black and Tan Terrier with Whippets and got a distinct Manchester type.
Until 1959 the Standard and the Toy were registered as separate breeds, though interbreeding was permitted.
Aside from size, the stated difference between the Standard and the Toy is ear shape.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 15-16 inches and weight as 12-22 pounds.

breeds.name: Manchester Terrier (Toy)

job.text: The Manchester Terrier (Toy) comes from a Manchester type developed to hunt rabbits and catch rats.

breeds.home: In a house, that work can look like a small dog who is quick to notice a scurry and who likes a short, fast chase.

facts.text: In the mid-1800s, local mill workers hunted rabbits with small hounds and set terriers on rats.
Breeders crossed the Black and Tan Terrier with Whippets to make one dog for both sports.
The breed reached the height of its popularity in the Victorian era.
Aside from size, the stated difference between the Standard and the Toy is ear shape.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10-12 inches and weight as under 12 pounds.

breeds.name: Mastiff

job.text: The Mastiff was developed in medieval England as a large hunting dog, used on game such as lion and deer.

breeds.home: In a house, that role can look like a big dog who stays with the household.

facts.text: Dogs of mastiff type are a running theme in the ancient history of Egypt, Asia, and Europe.
Julius Caesar wrote that his legions met some form of the breed during the Roman invasion of Britain in 55 b.c.
The Mastiff as we know it was developed in medieval England.
In the Canterbury Tales, Chaucer calls them Alaunts and says they were used to hunt the lion or the deer.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 30 inches & up (male), 27.5 inches & up (female) and weight as 160-230 pounds (male), 120-170 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Miniature American Shepherd

job.text: The Miniature American Shepherd was developed from small Australian Shepherds on the rodeo circuit as a compact companion for people traveling with horses.

breeds.home: In a house, that role can look like a dog who wants to go along, stay close to the family, and keep busy when people are moving.

facts.text: In the 1960s, small Australian Shepherds working the U.S. rodeo circuit were bred to make them still smaller.
The new breed was first called the Miniature Australian Shepherd.
It became especially popular with equestrians traveling to horse shows, because the size suited life on the road.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 14-18 inches (male), 13-17 inches (female) and weight as 20-40 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 2015 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Miniature Bull Terrier

job.text: The Miniature Bull Terrier was developed as a smaller dog for ratting above ground.

breeds.home: In a house, that ratting work can look like a dog who is curious about small movement along the floor and who likes to investigate corners.

facts.text: In the 1830s, Bulldogs were crossed with English terriers that are now extinct.
Breeders then worked on a smaller version to use as an above-ground ratter, rather than a terrier that burrows after quarry.
A Bulldog and the extinct White English Terrier were crossed to produce the Bull and Terrier, later called the Bull Terrier.
There were once Toy, Miniature, and Standard types, but the toy fell out of favor and only the Miniature and Standard remain.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10-14 inches and weight as 18-28 pounds.

breeds.name: Miniature Pinscher

job.text: The Miniature Pinscher was developed in Germany as a small companion and watchdog.

breeds.home: In a house, that watchdog role can look like a small dog who notices who comes to the door and wants the household to know.

facts.text: Breed historians accept that the Min Pin is a cross of the Dachshund and the Italian Greyhound, with the German Pinscher as another possible part.
The Miniature Pinscher is native to Germany.
It is often mistaken for a miniature Doberman Pinscher because the names and outlines are similar.
Despite the small size, the Miniature Pinscher is valued as a watchdog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10-12.5 inches and weight as 8-10 pounds.

breeds.name: Miniature Schnauzer

job.text: The Miniature Schnauzer was developed to catch rats and other vermin around the farm.

breeds.home: In a house, that ratting work can look like a dog who checks the edges of the yard and the corners of a room, and who wants a job to do.

facts.text: The Miniature Schnauzer was originally bred, like terriers, to catch rats and other vermin.
It was created by breeding Standard Schnauzers with Affenpinschers and Poodles.
Old-time German farmers bred the Standard Schnauzer down to miniature size.
The Standard Schnauzer is described as an all-around farm dog with a lineage going back to at least the 15th century.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 12-14 inches and weight as 11-20 pounds.

breeds.name: Mixed breed

job.text: A mixed-breed dog was not built for one kennel-club job. In a large owner survey, breed explained a small share of why individual dogs behave differently.

breeds.home: At home, start with the dog in front of you. A breed name, or a mix of them, is a small part of why he does what he does. When you can name an older job in the ancestry, that job is still the useful clue.

facts.text: Morrill and colleagues surveyed owners of 18,385 purebred and mixed-breed dogs and genotyped 2,155 dogs.
The paper reports that breed explains just 9% of behavioral variation in individuals.
Most behavioral traits in the study were heritable, with heritability above 25%.
The authors write that breed propensities align, weakly, with ancestral function.

They propose that behaviors people treat as typical of modern breeds come from thousands of years of polygenic adaptation that predates breed formation, and that modern breeds are distinguished primarily by aesthetic traits.

breeds.name: Mudi

job.text: The Mudi was developed as a small Hungarian sheepdog.

breeds.home: In a house, that herding work can look like a dog who wants to keep the family grouped and who is ready to move with people from place to place.

facts.text: The Mudi's early history runs with that of the Pumi and the Puli.
Around 1930, Dr. Deszö Fényesi, director of the museum in Balassagyarmat, was among the first to breed this small sheepdog on its own.
He is the person who named the breed Mudi.
The Mudi still herds in Hungary with shepherds and with flocks of up to 500 sheep.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 15-18.5 inches and weight as 18-29 pounds.

breeds.name: Neapolitan Mastiff

job.text: The Neapolitan Mastiff was developed as a guardian, and in the Roman Empire also worked as a war dog and gladiator.

breeds.home: In a house, that guardian role can look like a large dog who stays with the household and watches the door.

facts.text: The breed may go back as far as 700 b.c., and artifacts from several ancient civilizations show Mastino-like dogs.
In the Roman Empire these dogs worked as war dogs, gladiators, and guardians.
The breed is known for massiveness and loose folds of skin.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 26-31 inches (male), 24-29 inches (female) and weight as 150 pounds (male), 110 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 2004 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Nederlandse Kooikerhondje

job.text: The Nederlandse Kooikerhondje was developed to lure ducks into gun range by playing along the shore.

breeds.home: In a house, that tolling work can look like a dog who likes to play where people can see it, then bring a thrown toy back.

facts.text: The Kooikerhondje is a duck toller that lures waterfowl into gun range by playing at the lakeshore, and the wagging tail holds the ducks' attention.
The Kooikerhondje is believed to be an ancestor of the Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever.
Ancestors of the Kooiker can be seen in paintings by Vermeer, Steen, and other Dutch masters.
By the 1940s the breed was nearly extinct, and Baroness Van Hardenbroek van Ammerstol helped bring it back.
The AKC breed standard lists height as Dogs 16", Females 15" and weight as 20 - 30 lbs.

breeds.name: Newfoundland

job.text: The Newfoundland was developed as a shipboard dog to rescue people from the water, haul nets, and carry the catch.

breeds.home: In a house, that water-dog work can look like a dog who wants to swim, pull, and carry, and who stays close when the family is near water.

facts.text: Newfoundlands are born swimmers, with webbed feet, and strong enough to save a grown man from drowning.
They also earned their keep by hauling fishing nets ashore and carting the day's catch to market.
Most pedigree Newfoundlands, even in Newfoundland, descend from dogs born in England.
In Newfoundland and Labrador the breed is still used as a working dog to pull carts or carry burdens.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 28 inches (average male), 26 inches (average female) and weight as 130-150 pounds (male), 100-120 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Norfolk Terrier

job.text: The Norfolk Terrier was developed to catch rats and to bolt foxes.

breeds.home: In a house, that terrier work can look like a dog who wants to investigate burrows and corners and who is glad of a chance to work a problem through.

facts.text: Frank Jones, known as Roughrider, an English horseman of the early 20th century, developed little red terriers as ratters and fox bolters.
The Norwich, with ears up, and the Norfolk, with ears down, were once one breed.
The Norfolk was bred to go to ground after vermin and to catch a fox.
England recognized the Norfolk as a separate breed in 1964, and the AKC did so in 1979.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 9-10 inches and weight as 11-12 pounds.

breeds.name: Norwegian Buhund

job.text: The Norwegian Buhund was developed as a farm dog to herd and to guard the flock and the family.

breeds.home: In a house, that farm work can look like a dog who wants to stay with the household, keep the group together, and notice who comes onto the property.

facts.text: Buhunds sailed with the Vikings, whose raids reached across Europe about 1,200 years ago.
The name comes from the Norwegian word bu, meaning homestead or farm.
For centuries they served as herders, guardians of flock and family, and all-purpose farmhands.
The breed is also known as the Norsk Buhund and the Norwegian Sheepdog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 17-18.5 inches (male), 16-17.5 inches (female) and weight as 31-40 pounds (male), 26-35 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Norwegian Elkhound

job.text: The Norwegian Elkhound was developed to hunt large animals such as moose, wolves, and bear, and to haul supplies by sled.

breeds.home: In a house, that hunting work can look like a dog who wants a long outing, uses the nose, and stays close to the family on the trail.

facts.text: In its native land the Elkhound's main job was hunting large animals: moose, wolves, and even bear.
Elkhounds were also used as sled dogs to haul supplies over frozen ground.
The Elkhound is said to have been a companion of the Vikings.
Remnants of Norwegian Elkhounds dating back 5000 years have been found with Viking remains and weapons.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 20.5 inches (male), 19.5 inches (female) and weight as 55 pounds (male), 48 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Norwegian Lundehund

job.text: The Norwegian Lundehund was developed to climb cliffs and take puffins from narrow crevices.

breeds.home: In a house, that climbing work can look like a dog who wants to scramble, squeeze into small spaces, and carry what it finds.

facts.text: For centuries Lundehunds were bred on Vaeroy, a remote rocky island off the Norwegian coast, where puffins nest in cliff crevices.
Islanders depended on pickled puffin meat through long Arctic winters, and the Lundehund was how they reached the birds.
The dogs climbed the rock walls, worked into tiny passages, snatched the birds, and came back down the cliffs.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 13-15 inches (male), 12-14 inches (female) and weight as 15-18 lbs (male), 12-15 lbs (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 2011 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Norwich Terrier

job.text: The Norwich Terrier was developed to control rodents and to work in packs on foxhunts.

breeds.home: In a house, that terrier work can look like a dog who wants to check for a scurry and who is glad to do the job alongside people.

facts.text: The Norwich is one of the terriers bred to control Britain's rodents.
Norwiches were used in packs on foxhunts, which is why they tend to be more sociable than many terriers.
The breed was tied to Cambridge University, where owning a Norwich was an undergraduate fad in the late 1800s.
Until 1979 the name covered both the drop-eared and the prick-eared varieties.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10 inches and weight as 12 pounds.

breeds.name: Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever

job.text: The Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever was developed to lure ducks close by playing along the shore, then retrieve them.

breeds.home: In a house, that tolling work can look like a dog who wants to play fetch where the family can see it, and then carry the toy back.

facts.text: Canadian sportsmen bred retrievers to imitate foxes, whose color and quick movements draw waterfowl in.
The breed name comes from the Middle English word tollen, meaning to lure.
Nineteenth-century sportsmen bred this retriever in the Little River district of Yarmouth, Nova Scotia.
The breed is fashioned after the MicMac Indian Dog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 18-21 inches (male), 17-20 inches (female) and weight as 35-50 pounds.

breeds.name: Old English Sheepdog

job.text: The Old English Sheepdog was developed as a drover to move cattle and sheep from pasture to market.

breeds.home: In a house, that droving work can look like a dog who wants to move the family along and stay beside them as they go.

facts.text: They were bred as cattle drovers to move stock from pasture to market.
The makeup includes dogs of European and Russian ancestry, and the breed is not fully English.
The breed was most likely developed in the west of England, in Devon, Somerset, and the Duchy of Cornwall.
It first emerged at the beginning of the 18th century as a drover's dog, used to drive sheep and cattle to city markets.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 22 inches & up (male), 21 inches & up (female) and weight as 60-100 pounds.

breeds.name: Otterhound

job.text: The Otterhound was developed to hunt otters in packs and protect fish in rivers and ponds.

breeds.home: In a house, that hound work can look like a dog who wants to follow a scent, especially near water, and who is built for a long outing with the family.

facts.text: In medieval England a large otter population preyed on fish in rivers and stocked ponds.
Country squires and even kings kept those packs.
The hounds were so effective that river otters nearly disappeared and hunting them was outlawed.
Otterhounds appeared in the United States in 1903, and the first shown in America were at Claremont, New Hampshire, in 1907.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 27 inches (male), 24 inches (female) and weight as 115 pounds (male), 80 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Papillon

job.text: The Papillon was developed as a companion for noblewomen.

breeds.home: In a house, that companion role can look like a dog who wants to be with people and is ready to join whatever the family is doing.

facts.text: Papillons were originally bred as companions for noblewomen, and they appear in portraits of queens and princesses.
They began as toy spaniels and were once known as Dwarf Spaniels.
The name Papillon means butterfly in French.
Marie Antoinette admired Papillons.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 8-11 inches and weight as 5-10 pounds.

breeds.name: Parson Russell Terrier

job.text: The Parson Russell Terrier was developed to pursue foxes above and below ground alongside foxhounds.

breeds.home: In a house, that terrier work can look like a dog who wants to investigate holes and follow a scent with the family.

facts.text: The breed was developed in the south of England in the 1800s to pursue fox both above and below the ground.
The breed was named for the Reverend John Russell, called the Sporting Parson, whose passions were his ministry and his hunting dogs.
His terriers were bred to work with foxhounds in pursuit of the fox.
After his death, the name Jack Russell was applied to many different working terriers, not only dogs like his.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 14 inches (male), 13 inches (female) and weight as 13-17 pounds.

breeds.name: Pekingese

job.text: The Pekingese was developed as a companion for the royal families of ancient China.

breeds.home: In a house, that companion role can look like a dog who prefers to stay close and be carried along with the family.

facts.text: The Pekingese was created for the royal families of ancient China.
Peke-like dogs were living in Chinese luxury at least 1,300 years ago.
The breed was unknown in the West until 1860, when British troops entered Peking, and an army captain brought one back to Queen Victoria.
The breed was also called Lion Dog, Sun Dog, and Sleeve Dog, because it was carried in the sleeves of the imperial household.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 6-9 inches and weight as up to 14 pounds.

breeds.name: Pembroke Welsh Corgi

job.text: The Pembroke Welsh Corgi was developed to herd cattle and sheep.

breeds.home: In a house, that herding work can look like a dog who wants to move people along and keep the household grouped.

facts.text: The best weavers in Europe lived in Flanders.
In 1107 the king of Britain invited a community of weavers to live and work in Wales.
They brought dogs used to herd cattle and sheep, and those herders were the foundation of the Pembroke Welsh Corgi.
The Pembroke is the younger of the two corgi breeds and is a separate breed from the Cardigan.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10-12 inches and weight as up to 30 pounds (male), up to 28 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Petit Basset Griffon Vendéen

job.text: The Petit Basset Griffon Vendéen was developed to hunt game by scent in the rough country of coastal France.

breeds.home: In a house, that hound work can look like a dog who wants to follow a scent through brush and who keeps going when the cover gets thick.

facts.text: The PBGV was made to hunt among the rocks and dense underbrush of coastal France.
The eyebrows, beard, and mustache protect the face from thorns and thicket.
The breed is still bred in France, along with 27 other hound breeds, to hunt game by scent.
The line is traced to the sixteenth century and to the larger Griffon Vendéen.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 13-15 inches and weight as 25-40 pounds.

breeds.name: Pharaoh Hound

job.text: The Pharaoh Hound was developed in Malta to hunt rabbits.

breeds.home: In a house, that hunting work can look like a dog who wants a chance to chase and who comes alive when something moves in the open.

facts.text: Phoenician traders from what is today Lebanon sailed the Mediterranean about 2,500 years ago.
The prevailing theory is that Phoenicians brought the Pharaoh Hound to Malta, where it was used to hunt rabbits.
In 1979 the Pharaoh Hound was named the national hound of Malta.
Phoenicians are assumed to have spread Egyptian hounds through the ancient world, as far west as Britain.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23-25 inches (male), 21-24 inches (female) and weight as 45-55 pounds.

breeds.name: Plott Hound

job.text: The Plott Hound was developed in the mountains of North Carolina to hunt bear and other big game.

breeds.home: In a house, that hunting work can look like a dog who wants a long trail to follow with the family.

facts.text: Plotts descend from German Hanover hounds rather than English Foxhounds.
In 1750 the German immigrant Johannes Plott arrived in North Carolina with five Hanover hounds.
Plott settled in the mountains and hunted bears with his hounds.
His son Henry bred the family pack to local stock and produced the dog known as Plott's hound.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 20-25 inches (male), 20-23 inches (female) and weight as 50-60 pounds (male), 40-55 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Pointer

job.text: The Pointer was developed to find game and point it, first for coursing hounds and later for wing-shooting.

breeds.home: In a house, that pointing work can look like a dog who stops and indicates when a scent is worth attention, and who wants a big field to cover.

facts.text: Before rifles, British pointers hunted hares with coursing hounds: the Pointer found the prey and the hounds chased.
In the 1700s, with the rise of wing-shooting, the Pointer became a gundog for pointing and retrieving game birds.
In the 17th century, Pointers were used together with Greyhounds.
The first Pointers appeared in England about 1650.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25-28 inches (male), 23-26 inches (female) and weight as 55-75 pounds (male), 45-65 pounds (female).
