breeds.name: Polish Lowland Sheepdog

job.text: The Polish Lowland Sheepdog was developed as a flock dog by day and a guard dog by night.

breeds.home: In a house, that work can look like a dog who keeps the family grouped during the day and who notices the household at night.

facts.text: PONs are believed to come from Hunnic dogs bred to native stock in the region now known as Poland.
They were bred to be levelheaded flock dogs by day.
In the 1500s, traders brought them to Scotland, where they are thought to have contributed to the Bearded Collie.
They were also guard dogs by night.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 18-20 inches (male), 17-19 inches (female) and weight as 30-50 pounds.

breeds.name: Pomeranian

job.text: The Pomeranian was developed as a small companion from larger spitz-type sled dogs.

breeds.home: In a house, that companion role can look like a dog who wants to stay near people.

facts.text: The Pomeranian is a smaller relation of the spitz-type sled dogs of the Arctic.
In the 1800s Queen Victoria owned several Pomeranians and bred them.
She is credited with reducing the breed from about 30 pounds to the toy size.
The breed takes its name from Pomerania, now part of Poland and western Germany.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 6-7 inches and weight as 3-7 pounds.

breeds.name: Poodle

job.text: The Poodle was developed in Germany as a retrieving water dog for duck hunting.

breeds.home: In a house, that water work can look like a dog who wants to swim, retrieve, and stay busy with the family.

facts.text: The Poodle is the national dog of France, but there is no breed called the French Poodle.
In France the Poodle is called the Caniche, or duck dog.
The breed began as a duck hunter in Germany, where the word pudelin refers to splashing in water.
The Standard Poodle has been developed as a retrieving water dog for more than 400 years.
The AKC page for the Standard variety lists height as over 15 inches (standard) and weight as 60-70 pounds (male standard), 40-50 pounds (female standard).

breeds.name: Portuguese Podengo Pequeno

job.text: The Portuguese Podengo Pequeno was developed to hunt rabbits in rough country, alone or in small packs.

breeds.home: In a house, that hunting work can look like a dog who wants to search out a hiding spot and push something into the open.

facts.text: Ancestors are thought to have reached Portugal in antiquity with Phoenician, Roman, and Moorish traders and invaders.
The Portuguese adapted them to hunt rabbits in the craggy Iberian countryside.
Working alone or in small packs, they route rabbits out of hiding and into open country.
They have been called probably the world's smallest hunting dog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 8-12 inches and weight as 9-13 pounds.

breeds.name: Portuguese Water Dog

job.text: The Portuguese Water Dog was developed to herd fish into nets, retrieve lost tackle, and carry messages between ship and shore.

breeds.home: In a house, that water work can look like a dog who wants to swim, fetch, and stay with the family near the water.

facts.text: Along Portugal's coast these dogs herded fish into nets, retrieved lost tackle, and acted as messengers between ships and shore.
They rode in trawlers from the Atlantic waters of Portugal to the cold waters off Iceland.
The old fishing job faded with new technology, but the dogs are still used for water rescue.
The Portuguese Water Dog has webbed feet.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 20-23 inches (male), 17-21 inches (female) and weight as 42-60 pounds (male), 35-50 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Pug

job.text: The Pug was developed as a companion pet for the emperors of ancient China and their families.

breeds.home: In a house, that companion role looks like staying close to people and sharing ordinary daily life.

facts.text: The Pug was developed, along with the Pekingese and the Shih Tzu, as a pet for the emperor and his family.
Pugs left China for the West in the 1500s, carried by Dutch traders.
The Pug is one of the oldest breeds and has flourished since before 400 BC.
While she was imprisoned at Les Carmes, Josephine used her Pug Fortune to carry secret messages to her husband, Napoleon, under the dog's collar.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10-13 inches and weight as 14-18 pounds.

breeds.name: Puli

job.text: The Puli was developed to herd large flocks of sheep on the Hungarian plains.

breeds.home: At home, that herding work can look like gathering people or other pets and keeping the household together.

facts.text: Ancestors of the Puli were brought into Hungary by the Magyars and were similar to the Kuvasz and the Komondor.
Pulik are thought to have reached Europe about a thousand years ago with the same people who brought the Vizsla west.
They herded sheep on the Hungarian plains, and the corded coat protected them from hard winters.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 17 inches (male), 16 inches (female) and weight as 25-35 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 1936 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Pumi

job.text: The Pumi was developed as a Hungarian sheepdog by crossing the Puli with Western herding dogs and terriers.

breeds.home: In a house, that sheepdog job can look like watching the household and trying to move people or pets along.

facts.text: The Mudi, the Puli, and the Pumi are the three sheepdogs native to Hungary.
The Puli, thought to be the oldest of the three, was established in what is now Hungary around a.d. 800.
Between 300 and 400 years ago, the Puli was crossed with Western European herding dogs and terriers to produce the Pumi.
The name Pumi was first mentioned in 1815, describing a kind of sheepdog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 16-18.5 inches (male), 15-17.5 inches (female) and weight as 27-29 pounds (male), 22-24 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Pyrenean Shepherd

job.text: The Pyrenean Shepherd was developed to move flocks from one grazing area to another in the Pyrenees.

breeds.home: At home, moving a flock can look like a dog who keeps track of the family and steers them along together.

facts.text: These herding dogs were known among shepherds of the Pyrenees, the mountains that form the border between France and Spain.
Pyr Sheps often worked in tandem with the Great Pyrenees, the flock guardian of the same region.
Two Pyrenean Shepherds can manage a flock of 1000 sheep.
The breed first stood out beyond the Pyrenees through its service in World War I.

The AKC breed standard lists height as 15.5-18.5 inches (male rough-faced), 15-18 inches (female rough-faced), 15.5-21 inches (male smooth-faced), 15.5-20.5 inches (female smooth-faced) and weight as 15-30 pounds.

breeds.name: Rat Terrier

job.text: The Rat Terrier was bred to kill rats and to earn its keep as an all-purpose farm dog.

breeds.home: At home, that farm-ratter work can look like noticing small animals and staying busy around the house and yard.

facts.text: The name matches the work: these terriers were bred to kill rats.
On old farms a ratter mattered, because rodents in the grain could leave a family short of food for the winter.
Farmers also counted on them as hunting partners, watchdogs, henhouse guardians, and childhood playmates.
The AKC page for the Standard variety lists height as 10-13 inches (miniature), 13-18 inches (standard) and weight as 10-25 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 2013 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Redbone Coonhound

job.text: The Redbone Coonhound was developed by American settlers to hunt raccoons for meat and fur.

breeds.home: At home, trailing a raccoon can look like following a scent in the yard and giving voice when the trail is fresh.

facts.text: The Redbone is one of six hounds American settlers developed for a steady supply of raccoon meat and fur.
It descends from red foxhounds brought to America by Scottish immigrants in the late 1700s.
Red Irish Foxhounds were brought in before the Civil War.
Redbones are part of the nite hunt, a chase after the nocturnal raccoon.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 22-27 inches (male), 21-26 inches (female) and weight as 45-70 pounds.

breeds.name: Rhodesian Ridgeback

job.text: The Rhodesian Ridgeback was developed in southern Africa to hunt large game, including holding a lion at bay.

breeds.home: In a house, that hunting and watchdog work can look like a dog who ranges the property and stays watchful with the family.

facts.text: The breed was developed in southern Africa to hunt large game, including lions, and was once called the African Lion Hound.
These dogs were used to hold a lion at bay.
Dutch settlers called the Boers crossed European dogs with the native Khoi dog, which passed on the ridge.
The breed's formal development came hundreds of years later, from big-game hunter Cornelius van Rooyen.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25-27 inches (male), 24-26 inches (female) and weight as 85 pounds (male), 70 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Rottweiler

job.text: The Rottweiler descends from Roman drover dogs used to guide cattle and guard encampments.

breeds.home: In a house, driving stock and guarding a camp can look like a dog who stays with the family and watches the door and the yard.

facts.text: The Rottweiler is descended from Roman drover dogs.
The Romans used the dogs to guide cattle, their food on the road, and to guard encampments.
In the years 1901 to 1907, the Rottweiler again found favor as a police dog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 24-27 inches (male), 22-25 inches (female) and weight as 95-135 pounds (male), 80-100 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 1931 as the year this breed was recognized.

atts.text: American Temperament Test Society. Rottweilers: 85.0% pass rate, 6,216 dogs.
atts.note: A pass rate is a number, not a verdict. You decide what it means.

breeds.name: Russell Terrier

job.text: The Russell Terrier was developed as a fox-working dog that could run with the hounds and go to ground to bolt prey.

breeds.home: In a house, that fox-bolting job can look like a dog who runs hard and then squeezes into tight spaces after something that has gone to ground.

facts.text: The Russell and the Parson Russell share fox-working roots in the kennels of Rev. John Russell, the Sporting Parson, in the mid-1800s.
Russells were bred to run with the hounds and to be compact enough to go to ground and bolt prey.
The Russell Terrier began in England and was developed in Australia.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10-12 inches and weight as 9-15 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 2012 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Russian Toy

job.text: The Russian Toy began as an English Toy Terrier brought to Russia and kept as a small companion.

breeds.home: At home, that small companion role looks like a dog who stays beside people and joins everyday indoor life.

facts.text: The breed's history reaches the 18th century, when the English Toy Terrier arrived in Russia.
The Zoological Museum in St. Petersburg shows a small black and tan terrier specimen from 1716 to 1725.
The specimen's inscription names the dog Lisetta and says it belonged personally to Peter the Great.
In 18th century Russia the breed was a popular companion of the aristocracy.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 8-11 inches and weight as Up to 6.5 pounds.

breeds.name: Russian Tsvetnaya Bolonka

job.text: The Russian Tsvetnaya Bolonka was created in Leningrad in the 1950s as a decorative companion dog.

breeds.home: In a house, that companion role looks like a small dog who lives close to people through the day.

facts.text: The Russian Colored Lapdog was begun in the 1950s.
In 1951, dog lovers in Leningrad were part of creating the Russian Colored Lapdog.
The coat took shape because grooming products were scarce in Russia.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 11 inches and weight as 6 - 9 pounds.
The AKC breeds-by-year list gives 2026 as the year this breed became registrable.

breeds.name: Saint Bernard

job.text: Monks at a hospice in the Alps developed the Saint Bernard to find and rescue travelers buried in snow.

breeds.home: In a house, that people-finding work can look like a dog who stays near the family and wants to know where they are.

facts.text: In 1050, Bernard of Menthon founded a hospice in the Alps to help pilgrims on the way to Rome.
The monks developed dogs able to locate and rescue travelers buried by drifts and avalanches.
Dogs of the Great St. Bernard Pass did not carry casks of brandy around their necks.
The Saint most likely developed from heavy Asian Molosser stock brought to Switzerland by Roman armies.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 28-30 inches (males), 26-28 inches (female) and weight as 140-180 pounds (male), 120-140 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Saluki

job.text: The Saluki was developed as a sighthound used to track and bring down gazelle.

breeds.home: In a house, that coursing job can look like a sudden run on open, fenced ground and a sharp eye for movement.

facts.text: Experts say the Saluki may go back as far as 7000 b.c.
Salukis were favorites of Egyptian pharaohs and of Alexander the Great.
Arabs used the Saluki mainly to track and bring down gazelle.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23-28 inches (male), considerably smaller (female) and weight as 40-65 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 1929 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Samoyed

job.text: The Samoyed was developed by the Samoyede people to herd and guard reindeer and to pull sleds.

breeds.home: In a house, herding and sled work can look like a dog who stays close to the family, watches over them, and likes to pull when out on foot.

facts.text: Samoyed is taken from Samoyede, the name of a semi-nomadic people who moved from Asia to Siberia.
The Samoyede first used the dogs to hunt reindeer, then trained them to herd and protect the herds.
The dogs also sledged heavy loads across Siberia.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 21-23.5 inches (male), 19-21 inches (female) and weight as 45-65 pounds (male), 35-50 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 1906 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Schipperke

job.text: The Schipperke was developed as a shipboard ratter on the canals of the Low Countries and as a watchdog on barges and in shops.

breeds.home: In a house, that ratting and watchdog work can look like a dog who notices small animals and speaks up when someone arrives.

facts.text: The Schipperke comes from late medieval Belgium.
The breed became known as a shipboard ratter on the canals of the Low Countries.
It also worked as a watchdog on barges and in city shops.
Sailors and shopkeepers in Brussels and Antwerp called the dog schipperke, Flemish for little captain.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 11-13 inches (male), 10-12 inches (female) and weight as 10-16 pounds.

breeds.name: Scottish Deerhound

job.text: The Scottish Deerhound was developed to pursue and bring down the wild red deer.

breeds.home: In a house, that coursing work can look like a dog who wants open space for a long run.

facts.text: Evidence suggests large deer-stalking hounds were in Scotland before the Scots arrived in the ninth century.
Clan chieftains used packs of these hounds to pursue wild red deer, described as swift 400-pound animals with heavy antlers.
Hunters usually run Scottish Deerhounds singly or in pairs.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 30-32 inches (male), 28 inches & up (female) and weight as 85-110 pounds (male), 75-95 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 1886 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Scottish Terrier

job.text: The Scottish Terrier was developed to hunt rats, foxes, and badgers in the Scottish Highlands.

breeds.home: At home, that hunting job can look like a dog who digs, checks burrows, and follows a scent in the yard.

facts.text: The Scottie was developed on the craggy Scottish Highlands to hunt rats, foxes, and badgers.
Among the Highland terriers, the Scottie is thought to be the oldest.
John Naylor is credited as the first person to bring the Scottie to this country.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10 inches and weight as 19-22 pounds (male), 18-21 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 1885 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Sealyham Terrier

job.text: The Sealyham Terrier was developed in Wales to quarry badger, fox, and otter.

breeds.home: At home, that den work can look like a dog who investigates holes and burrows around the yard.

facts.text: Army captain John Edwardes developed the breed at his Sealy Ham estate in Wales.
The breed name honors the Sealy Ham estate on the Seal River in southwestern Wales.
The strain was noted for quarrying badger, fox, and otter.
Sources believe it came from crosses of the Corgi, Dandie Dinmont, West Highland White, Wirehaired Fox Terrier, and Bull Terrier.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10.5 inches and weight as 23-24 pounds (male), slightly less (females).

breeds.name: Shetland Sheepdog

job.text: The Shetland Sheepdog was developed to herd sheep, ponies, and poultry on farms in the Shetland Islands.

breeds.home: At home, that herding job can look like a dog who gathers the family and watches anything that moves.

facts.text: On farms in the Shetland Islands, Shelties helped herd the sheep, the ponies, and the chickens.
The breed is related to the larger Collie and was kept for similar work.
Lord Scott, brought from Shetland by John G. Sherman, Jr. of New York, was the first Sheltie the AKC registered, in 1911.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 13-16 inches and weight as 15-25 pounds.

breeds.name: Shiba Inu

job.text: The Shiba Inu was developed to hunt in the rugged mountains of Japan.

breeds.home: In a house, that hunting background can look like a dog who watches the ground and wants room to range.

facts.text: The breed is named for its history as a hunter in the rugged mountains of Japan.
Shiba means brushwood, either the mountain brush or the dog's reddish color, and Inu means dog.
The Shiba has been around since 300 b.c.
Among Japan's dogs, the Shiba is considered both the oldest and the smallest.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 14.5-16.5 inches (male), 13.5-15.5 inches (female) and weight as 23 pounds (male), 17 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Shih Tzu

job.text: The Shih Tzu was developed in the palace of the Chinese emperor as a lap companion.

breeds.home: In a house, that lap-companion role looks like sitting with people and staying near them indoors.

facts.text: The Shih Tzu took shape in the Chinese emperor's palace, where imperial breeders made the dog.
The breed was made centuries ago from Tibetan breeding stock.
Shih Tzu means lion, and the dogs were bred in court.
For most of the Ming Dynasty, the Shih Tzu lived as a house pet.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 9-10.5 inches and weight as 9-16 pounds.

breeds.name: Siberian Husky

job.text: The Siberian Husky was developed by the Chukchi people of northeastern Asia as an endurance sled dog and family companion.

breeds.home: At home, that sled-dog work can look like a dog who wants to pull and cover ground with the family, and who lives as a companion in the house.

facts.text: The Chukchi people of northeastern Asia kept these dogs as family companions and as endurance sled dogs.
The sled dog was meant to travel long distances at a moderate speed, carrying a light load in low temperatures.
In 1910, John "Iron Man" Johnson drove a Siberian Husky team to win the 400-mile All Alaska Sweepstakes Race.
Leonhard Seppala both bred and raced dogs of this breed.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 21-23.5 inches (male), 20-22 inches (female) and weight as 45-60 pounds (male), 35-50 pounds (female).

atts.text: American Temperament Test Society. Huskies: 86.7% pass rate.
atts.note: A pass rate is a number, not a verdict. You decide what it means.

breeds.name: Silky Terrier

job.text: The Silky Terrier was created in Australia in the early 20th century from Yorkshire Terriers and Australian Terriers.

breeds.home: In a house, a dog made from those small terriers can live at close range with the family.

facts.text: Australian breeders made the Silky mainly from Yorkies and Australian Terriers.
Cairn, Dandie Dinmont, and Skye terriers, brought to Australia by English settlers, may also be in the background.
The breed was first called the Sydney Silky Terrier, then the Australian Silky Terrier in 1955.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 9-10 inches and weight as around 10 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 1959 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Skye Terrier

job.text: The Skye Terrier was developed by farmers on the island of Skye to control foxes and badgers.

breeds.home: In a house, that farm work can look like a dog who investigates cover and watches the edges of the property.

facts.text: Skye is the largest and most northerly of Scotland's Inner Hebrides.
In the 1600s, farmers on the island bred a hard-coated terrier to control foxes and badgers.
Queen Victoria championed the breed in the late 19th century.
Greyfriars Bobby, a Skye Terrier, lay on his master John Gray's grave for fourteen years and left only for food.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10 inches (male), 9.5 inches (female) and weight as 35-45 pounds (male), slightly lighter (female).

breeds.name: Sloughi

job.text: The Sloughi was developed to course game across desert country.

breeds.home: At home, coursing over open ground can look like a fast run in a large fenced area and close attention to anything that moves.

facts.text: Sloughi-type hounds were hunting companions of Egyptian nobles, Berber kings, and nomadic chieftains.
Those packs coursed game across wide stretches of desert.
One theory says Berber cavalrymen with Hannibal may have brought the Sloughi into Europe when he crossed the Alps.
The Sloughi comes from North Africa.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 26-29 inches (male), 24-27 inches (female) and weight as 40 -65 pounds.

breeds.name: Smooth Fox Terrier

job.text: The Smooth Fox Terrier was developed to ride to the hunt and bolt a fox that had gone underground.

breeds.home: In a house, that earth-dog job can look like investigating holes and tight spaces and staying with the task until it is finished.

facts.text: On a hunt the terriers rode in saddlebags and were released when the fox went underground.
The dog's job was to harry a fox in its hole until the fox bolted.
The Smooth is thought to come from the Old English Terrier, smooth-coated Black and Tan terriers, Bull Terriers, Greyhounds, and Beagles.
Herbert Hoover's two Fox Terriers were named Big Ben and Sonnie.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 15½ inches and weight as 18 pounds (male), 15-17 (female).

breeds.name: Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier

job.text: The Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier was developed as an Irish farm dog for ratting, guarding, herding, and bird-dogging.

breeds.home: At home, those farm chores can look like a busy day around the yard, followed by time beside the family.

facts.text: The Wheaten shares its ancestry with the Kerry Blue and the Irish Terrier, and the three were bred for similar work.
On the farm a Wheaten was expected to rat, guard the chicken coop, herd, or bird-dog.
Wheatens first reached the United States in the 1940s with Lydia Vogel of Massachusetts.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 18-19 inches (male), 17-18 inches (female) and weight as 35-40 pounds (male), 30-35 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 1973 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Spanish Water Dog

job.text: The Spanish Water Dog was developed both to retrieve waterfowl and to herd sheep.

breeds.home: In a house, that dual job can look like a dog who wants to swim and retrieve, and who also keeps the family grouped the way a herder moves stock.

facts.text: One theory says the Moors brought the breed from North Africa when they occupied Spain.
Another account says Turkish traders introduced it to Spain, which is why an old nickname was the Turkish Dog.
It was always used as both a waterfowl retriever and a sheepherder.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 17.5-19.75 inches (male), 15.75-18 inches (female) and weight as 40-49 pounds (male), 31-40 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 2015 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Spinone Italiano

job.text: The Spinone Italiano was developed in Italy's Piedmont to hunt beside people and to retrieve on land or water.

breeds.home: In a house, that hunting partnership can look like a dog who wants to be out with people, using its nose and bringing things back.

facts.text: The name Spinone refers to pino, the thorny undergrowth of Italy's Piedmont.
All-purpose Spinoni were first bred to work beside huntsmen on the hills of Alpine Italy.
The breed is estimated to include coarsehaired Italian Setters, dogs left by Greek traders and others from the Adriatic coast, and the White Mastiff.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23-27 inches (male), 22-25 inches (female) and weight as In direct proportion to size and structure of a dog.
The American Kennel Club lists 2000 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Staffordshire Bull Terrier

job.text: The Staffordshire Bull Terrier was developed from Bulldog and terrier crosses when dogfighting was treated as a sport.

breeds.home: In a house, the strength and quickness those crosses were built for can look like an active dog who stays in the middle of family life.

facts.text: The Stafford is grouped with the Bull Terrier, the Miniature Bull Terrier, and the AmStaff as bull-type terriers with a similar backstory.
Breeders crossed the Bulldog's strength and jaws with the terrier's quickness.
The old-fashioned Bulldog was used in bear-baiting and bull-baiting as early as the mid-sixteenth century.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 14-16 inches and weight as 28-38 pounds (male), 24-34 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 1974 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Standard Schnauzer

job.text: The Standard Schnauzer was developed as a German farm dog for ratting, herding, guarding, and hunting.

breeds.home: In a house, that farm-dog mix can look like a dog who watches the yard, notices small animals, and stays involved with the household.

facts.text: The Standard is the original Schnauzer and the parent of the Miniature and the Giant.
On farms they worked as ratters, herders, guardians, and hunters.
Dogs like today's Schnauzer appear in German artwork of the 15th and 16th centuries.
They were first called Wire-Haired Pinschers and, by the 1900s, Schnauzers, a name that refers to the bearded muzzle.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 18.5-19.5 inches (male), 17.5-18.5 inches (female) and weight as 35-50 pounds (male), 30-45 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Sussex Spaniel

job.text: The Sussex Spaniel was developed to hunt feathered game through the heavy clay, brush, and hedgerows of Sussex.

breeds.home: In a house, that close-cover hunting job can look like a dog who works low to the ground, uses its voice, and stays near people.

facts.text: In the 1700s, sportsmen in Sussex developed a short-legged spaniel to hunt feathered game.
Because the dog was built low and the cover was high, the Sussex used barks and babbling to show huntsmen where it was.
The breed is named for Sussex, England, where the first important kennel of these dogs was established.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 13-15 inches and weight as 35-45 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 1878 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Swedish Vallhund

job.text: The Swedish Vallhund was developed as a cattle dog and all-purpose farm dog in western Sweden.

breeds.home: In a house, that cattle-dog work can look like a dog who moves with the family and tries to keep everyone going as a group.

facts.text: The Vallhund is thought to be a cross of Scandinavian spitz dogs and Welsh corgis.
For centuries these dogs were cattle herders and general farmhands in western Sweden.
The breed is also called the Vastgotaspets and the Swedish Cattledog.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 12.5-13.75 inches (male), 11.5-12.75 inches (female) and weight as 20-35 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 2007 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Teddy Roosevelt Terrier

job.text: The Teddy Roosevelt Terrier was developed in the United States to clear homes and farms of vermin.

breeds.home: In a house, that vermin-clearing job can look like a dog who checks the corners of the home, the shed, and the yard.

facts.text: The breed was developed in the United States from small and medium dogs that came with early American immigrants.
Most of those dogs were small hunting and terrier types whose job was to clear vermin from the home and the farm.
The mix probably included the Smooth Fox Terrier, Manchester Terrier, Beagle, Whippet, Italian Greyhound, and the extinct White English Terrier.
The Teddy Roosevelt was originally the short-legged form of the Rat Terrier, known as Type B.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 8-14 inches and weight as 8-25 pounds.

breeds.name: Tibetan Mastiff

job.text: The Tibetan Mastiff was developed as a guardian in the Himalayas.

breeds.home: In a house, that guardian role can look like watching the home and staying between the family and anything unfamiliar.

facts.text: For millennia these dogs were guardians of the Himalayas.
They are thought to be the progenitor of all modern mastiffs.
Early travelers to Tibet were sometimes given these dogs, which were then used to create mastiff breeds of the Middle East and Europe.
The AKC breed standard lists height as minimum 26 inches (male), minimum 24 inches (female) and weight as 90-150 pounds (male), 70-120 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 2006 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Tibetan Spaniel

job.text: The Tibetan Spaniel was kept by Buddhist monks as a companion and as a watchdog on monastery walls.

breeds.home: In a house, that sentinel job can look like a dog who takes a high seat near a window and watches what comes and goes.

facts.text: Buddhist monks kept Tibbies mainly as companions and as watchdogs working in tandem with the Tibetan Mastiff.
They sat atop the monastery walls and scanned the horizon.
As the breed became more highly regarded, dogs were sent as gifts to the palaces of China and other Buddhist countries.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 10 inches and weight as 9-15 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 1983 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Tibetan Terrier

job.text: The Tibetan Terrier was developed in Tibet as a companion, watchdog, herder, and flock guardian.

breeds.home: In a house, that companion and watchdog role can look like a dog who stays with the family and notices who comes and goes.

facts.text: Westerners hung the name terrier on this Asian dog, and the name stuck.
The dogs are linked with Buddhist monasteries and the Dalai Lama.
Nearly 2000 years ago, lamas were raising the Tibetan Terrier in monasteries.
The breed is best known as a companion and watchdog, and it has also worked as a herder and flock guardian.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 14-17 inches and weight as 18-30 pounds (male), slightly smaller (female).

breeds.name: Toy Fox Terrier

job.text: The Toy Fox Terrier was developed in the United States from Smooth Fox Terriers and toy breeds, and it began as a barnyard ratter.

breeds.home: In a house, that barnyard ratting job can look like a small, busy dog who investigates corners and crannies.

facts.text: In the early 20th century, American breeders crossed Smooth Fox Terrier runts with toy dogs, including Chihuahuas and Italian Greyhounds.
Another account includes the Miniature Pinscher among those toy breeds.
They began as barnyard ratters and soon worked as circus trick dogs.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 8.5-11.5 inches and weight as 4 - 9 lbs.
The American Kennel Club lists 2003 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Treeing Walker Coonhound

job.text: The Treeing Walker Coonhound was developed to trail quarry until it climbs a tree and then bark until the hunter arrives.

breeds.home: In a house, that treeing work can look like following a scent through the yard and barking steadily once the trail ends.

facts.text: Treeing means the hound follows a scent until the quarry climbs a tree.
The hound then stays under the tree and barks until the hunter arrives.
Walker is Thomas Walker of Virginia, a central figure in the breed's early development in the mid-1700s.
Coonhound means a dog developed to tree raccoons and, sometimes, bigger game.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 22-27 inches (male), 20-25 inches (female) and weight as 50-70 pounds.

breeds.name: Vizsla

job.text: The Vizsla was developed by the Magyars as a swift, all-purpose hunting dog.

breeds.home: In a house, that all-purpose hunting job can look like a dog who wants to spend the day's outing working with people.

facts.text: The Magyars, Asian riders on horseback, developed the Vizsla after they swept into Europe following the fall of the Roman Empire.
The Magyar people left the Russian steppes in the mid-800s.
Vizslas became known as swift, all-purpose hunting dogs.
By the end of World War I the Vizsla was nearly extinct.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 22-24 inches (male), 21-23 inches (female) and weight as 55-60 pounds (male), 44-55 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Weimaraner

job.text: The Weimaraner was developed in the German town of Weimar to hunt big game and later to point and retrieve birds.

breeds.home: At home, that pointing and retrieving work can look like a dog who marks what it finds and brings it back to people.

facts.text: Noblemen in Weimar developed the breed to hunt big game such as bears and wolves.
When those predators grew fewer, the Weimaraner became a hunter that points and retrieves game birds.
Grand Duke Karl August, who held court in Weimar, was the key figure in the breed's early history.
The breed dates to the early 19th century in Germany.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 25-27 inches (male), 23-25 inches (female) and weight as 70-90 pounds (male), 55-75 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Welsh Springer Spaniel

job.text: The Welsh Springer Spaniel descends from the original spaniels of the Iberian Peninsula, described as the oldest spaniel line in Britain.

breeds.home: In a house, that old spaniel background can look like a dog who wants to be outdoors in the company of people.

facts.text: Leading authorities call Welsh Springers the oldest of Britain's spaniels, descended from the spaniels of the Iberian Peninsula.
The word spaniel comes from Spaniard.
Dogs of this type appear in British art and literature going back some 250 years b.c.
Welsh and English Springers became separate breeds in the early 1900s.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 18-19 inches (male), 17-18 inches (female) and weight as 40-55 pounds (male), 35-50 pounds (female).

breeds.name: Welsh Terrier

job.text: The Welsh Terrier was developed to hunt fox, otter, and badger in the mountains of northern Wales.

breeds.home: In a house, that earth-dog job can look like digging and investigating holes and thick cover around the yard.

facts.text: By sometime in the 1700s, the Welsh Terrier was taking the form known today.
They were bred to hunt fox, otter, and badger in the remote mountains of northern Wales.
The Welsh Terrier descends from old English wirehaired black-and-tan sporting dogs.
The Welsh Terrier had a reputation for work on badger, fox, and otter.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 15 inches (male), porportionally smaller (female) and weight as 20 pounds (male), proportionally smaller (female).

breeds.name: West Highland White Terrier

job.text: The West Highland White Terrier was developed in Scotland to reduce the rodent population.

breeds.home: In a house, that rodent-control job can look like a dog who investigates holes and keeps an eye on small animals around the home.

facts.text: In the 1700s the Malcom clan bred these terriers on the Poltalloch estate, and the breed was sometimes called the Poltalloch Terrier.
West Highland in the name refers to the northwest of Scotland, where the breed made its name.
The Scottie, Cairn, Dandie Dinmont, and West Highland White are branches of the same stock.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 11 inches (male), 10 inches (female) and weight as 15-20 pounds.
The American Kennel Club lists 1908 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Whippet

job.text: The Whippet was developed in England for vermin hunting and racing.

breeds.home: In a house, that racing and hunting background can look like a short burst of speed in a fenced space.

facts.text: The Whippet is a mix of Greyhounds, terriers, and Italian Greyhounds and comes from England.
Working people used Whippets for vermin hunting and racing.
The Whippet story begins in Victorian England, where north-country coal miners spent days off racing dogs and hunting rabbits.
The Whippet reached north-central Massachusetts with mill workers.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 19-22 inches (male), 18-21 inches (female) and weight as 25-40 pounds.

breeds.name: Wire Fox Terrier

job.text: The Wire Fox Terrier was developed to bolt the fox from its lair so the hunt could continue.

breeds.home: In a house, that earth-dog job can look like investigating dens and tight spaces and staying on the task.

facts.text: Fox Terriers took shape in the late 1700s, during the heyday of British foxhunts, and their job was to bolt the fox from its lair.
The coat is mostly white, and red is not allowed, so the dog is not mistaken for a fox during a hunt.
Paintings show that both the wire and smooth coats were around by the middle of the 18th century.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 15½ inches and weight as 18 pounds (male), 15-17 (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 1885 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Wirehaired Pointing Griffon

job.text: Eduard Korthals developed the Wirehaired Pointing Griffon to point game on land and retrieve it from water.

breeds.home: At home, that pointing and water work can look like a dog who wants to be outdoors with people, will swim, and brings objects back.

facts.text: Eduard Korthals, a Dutch banker's son, was one of the Continental sportsmen breeding versatile hunting dogs.
By crossing several breeds, Korthals got a dog that could point on land, retrieve from water, and had webbed toes for swimming.
Korthals refined the breed while working in Germany and then in France.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 22-24 inches (male), 20-22 inches (female) and weight as 50-70 pounds (male), 35-50 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 1887 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Wirehaired Vizsla

job.text: The Wirehaired Vizsla was developed in Hungary in the 1930s so hunters would have a Vizsla's drive in a sturdier body and a denser coat.

breeds.home: In a house, that hunting job can look like a dog who wants to work outdoors with people and keep going when the weather turns cold or the ground is rough.

facts.text: Wirehaired Vizslas were created in the 1930s.
Hungarian hunters and falconers wanted the Vizsla's drive with a sturdier frame and a denser coat for hard ground and cold weather.
They made the breed by crossing Vizslas with German Wirehaired Pointers.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 23-25 inches (male), 21.5-23 inches (female) and weight as 55-65 pounds (male), 45-55 pounds (female).
The American Kennel Club lists 2014 as the year this breed was recognized.

breeds.name: Xoloitzcuintli

job.text: The Xoloitzcuintli was kept by the Aztecs as a sacred companion and guide, and in modern times as a watchdog and companion.

breeds.home: In a house, that companion and watchdog work can look like a dog who stays near the family and notices arrivals.

facts.text: In Mexico the Xolo is a national treasure with a history of at least 5,000 years.
Columbus and other European explorers wrote about these hairless dogs.
The Aztecs named the breed for Xolotl, a god shown with a dog's head.
The Aztecs held Xolos sacred and often sacrificed and buried them with their owners to serve as guides in the next world.

The AKC page for the Standard variety lists height as 10-14 inches (toy), 14-18 inches (miniature), 18-23 inches (standard) and weight as 10-15 pounds (toy), 15-30 pounds (miniature), 30-55 pounds (standard).

breeds.name: Yorkshire Terrier

job.text: The Yorkshire Terrier was developed by Scottish weavers to hunt vermin in the fabric mills of Yorkshire.

breeds.home: In a house, that mill-ratting job can look like a small dog who hunts through corners and stays alert to little movements.

facts.text: Scottish weavers who moved to Yorkshire in the 19th century bred the Yorkie to hunt vermin in the fabric mills.
The breed was developed in the mid-1800s in the English counties of Yorkshire and Lancashire.
The Yorkie traces to the Waterside Terrier, also called a weaver dog.
During World War II, a Yorkie named Smoky carried a communications wire through an underground tunnel.
The AKC breed standard lists height as 7-8 inches and weight as 7 pounds.
